## Delete a Deployment

<a id="opIddeleteDeployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v13/deployments/dpl_5WJWYSyB7BpgTj3EuwF37WMRBXBtPQ2iTMJHJBJyRfd \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v13/deployments/{id}`

This API allows you to delete a deployment, either by supplying its `id` in the URL or the `url` of the deployment as a query parameter. You can obtain the ID, for example, by listing all deployments.

<h3 id="delete-a-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the deployment to be deleted|
|url|query|string|false|A Deployment or Alias URL. In case it is passed, the ID will be ignored|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "state": "DELETED",
  "uid": "dpl_5WJWYSyB7BpgTj3EuwF37WMRBXBtPQ2iTMJHJBJyRfd"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The deployment was successfully deleted|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|

## createObservabilityQuery

<a id="opIdcreateObservabilityQuery"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/observability/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "metric": "string",
    "scope": {},
    "aggregation": "string",
    "groupBy": [
      "string"
    ],
    "filter": "string",
    "limit": 0,
    "orderBy": "string",
    "orderDirection": "asc",
    "granularity": {},
    "startTime": "string",
    "endTime": "string",
    "bucketTimezone": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/observability/query`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "metric": "string",
  "scope": {},
  "aggregation": "string",
  "groupBy": [
    "string"
  ],
  "filter": "string",
  "limit": 0,
  "orderBy": "string",
  "orderDirection": "asc",
  "granularity": {},
  "startTime": "string",
  "endTime": "string",
  "bucketTimezone": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createobservabilityquery-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» metric|body|string|true|Metric id|
|» scope|body|object|true|Owner or project scope for the query|
|» aggregation|body|string|false|Aggregation function to apply. Some aggregations require a dimension: use <agg>/<dimension>, for example unique/visitor_id.|
|» groupBy|body|[string]|false|Dimensions to group results by. JSON dimensions support nested refs, for example event_data/checkout_step. Nested keys containing characters that OData cannot parse as an identifier, such as '-', spaces, quotes, or '/', must be wrapped in single quotes (escape embedded single quotes by doubling them), for example flags/'enable-comments-view' or event_data/'some property''s/value'.|
|» filter|body|string|false|Filter to apply to the query. JSON dimensions support nested refs, for example event_data/checkout_step eq 'payment'. Nested keys containing characters that OData cannot parse as an identifier, such as '-', spaces, quotes, or '/', must be wrapped in single quotes (escape embedded single quotes by doubling them), for example flags/'enable-comments-view' eq true or event_data/'some property''s/value' eq true.|
|» limit|body|number|false|Maximum number of results|
|» orderBy|body|string|false|Rollup column to order grouped results by. Use the generated rollup key for the requested metric and aggregation. Defaults to the query engine count rollup.|
|» orderDirection|body|string|false|Direction to order grouped results by. Defaults to desc.|
|» granularity|body|object|false|Time bucket size|
|» startTime|body|string|false|Start timestamp|
|» endTime|body|string|false|End timestamp|
|» bucketTimezone|body|string|false|IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Paris) used only to align calendar buckets (1d/1mo) to that zone's day/month boundaries. startTime/endTime and all output timestamps are always UTC. No effect on sub-day granularities.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» orderDirection|asc|
|» orderDirection|desc|

## Get TLD price data

<a id="opIdgetTldPrice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/registrar/tlds/string/price \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/registrar/tlds/{tld}/price`

Get price data for a specific TLD. This only reflects base prices for the given TLD. Premium domains may have different prices. Use the [Get price data for a domain](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/reference/endpoints/domains-registrar/get-price-data-for-a-domain) endpoint to get the price data for a specific domain.

<h3 id="get-tld-price-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

<h1 id="vercel-api-domains">domains</h1>

## Get a Domain's configuration

<a id="opIdgetDomainConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v6/domains/example.com/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v6/domains/{domain}/config`

Get a Domain's configuration.

<h3 id="get-a-domains-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|path|string|true|The name of the domain.|
|projectIdOrName|query|string|false|The project id or name that will be associated with the domain. Use this when the domain is not yet associated with a project.|
|strict|query|string|false|When true, the response will only include the nameservers assigned directly to the specified domain. When false and there are no nameservers assigned directly to the specified domain, the response will include the nameservers of the domain's parent zone.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|strict|true|
|strict|false|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acceptedChallenges": [
    "dns-01"
  ],
  "configuredBy": "A",
  "recommendedCNAME": [
    {
      "rank": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "recommendedIPv4": [
    {
      "rank": 0,
      "value": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "misconfigured": false
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-domains-configuration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="get-a-domains-configuration-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acceptedChallenges|[string]|true|none|Which challenge types the domain can use for issuing certs.|
|configuredBy|string \| null|true|none|How we see the domain's configuration. - `CNAME`: Domain has a CNAME pointing to Vercel. - `A`: Domain's A record is resolving to Vercel. - `http`: Domain is resolving to Vercel but may be behind a Proxy. - `dns-01`: Domain is not resolving to Vercel but dns-01 challenge is enabled. - `null`: Domain is not resolving to Vercel.|
|recommendedCNAME|[object]|true|none|Recommended CNAMEs for the domain. rank=1 is the preferred value to use.|
|» rank|number|true|none|none|
|» value|string|true|none|none|
|recommendedIPv4|[object]|true|none|Recommended IPv4s for the domain. rank=1 is the preferred value(s) to use. Only using 1 ip value is acceptable.|
|» rank|number|true|none|none|
|» value|[string]|true|none|none|
|misconfigured|boolean|true|none|Whether or not the domain is configured AND we can automatically generate a TLS certificate.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|acceptedChallenges|dns-01|
|acceptedChallenges|http-01|
|configuredBy|A|
|configuredBy|CNAME|
|configuredBy|dns-01|
|configuredBy|http|
|configuredBy|null|
|misconfigured|false|
|misconfigured|true|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Get Domain Verification Record

<a id="opIdgetDomainVerificationRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/domains/example.com/verification \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v9/domains/{domain}/verification`

Get the TXT verification record needed to claim ownership of a domain for the authenticated team. The caller must add this TXT record to `_vercel.{domain}` in their DNS configuration, then call POST /domains/:domain/claim to complete the ownership transfer.

<h3 id="get-domain-verification-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|path|string|true|The domain name to get the verification record for|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "txtRecord": "string",
  "verificationDomain": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-domain-verification-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the TXT record needed to verify domain ownership.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="get-domain-verification-record-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|txtRecord|string|true|none|none|
|verificationDomain|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Claim Domain Ownership

<a id="opIdclaimDomainOwnership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/domains/example.com/claim \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v9/domains/{domain}/claim`

Claim ownership of a domain for the authenticated team by verifying a TXT record. The caller must first add a TXT record to `_vercel.{domain}` (obtained from GET /domains/:domain/verification), then call this endpoint to complete the ownership transfer. If the TXT record is verified, the domain ownership will be transferred to the caller's team, even if the domain is currently owned by another user or team.

<h3 id="claim-domain-ownership-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|path|string|true|The domain name to claim ownership of|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "domain": {
    "boughtAt": 1613602938882,
    "createdAt": 1613602938882,
    "creator": {
      "id": "ZspSRT4ljIEEmMHgoDwKWDei",
      "username": "vercel_user",
      "email": "demo@example.com"
    },
    "customNameservers": [
      "ns1.nameserver.net",
      "ns2.nameserver.net"
    ],
    "echMode": "auto",
    "expiresAt": 0,
    "id": "EmTbe5CEJyTk2yVAHBUWy4A3sRusca3GCwRjTC1bpeVnt1",
    "intendedNameservers": [
      "ns1.vercel-dns.com",
      "ns2.vercel-dns.com"
    ],
    "name": "example.com",
    "nameservers": [
      "ns1.nameserver.net",
      "ns2.nameserver.net"
    ],
    "renew": true,
    "serviceType": "zeit.world",
    "teamId": "string",
    "transferredAt": 1613602938882,
    "transferStartedAt": 1613602938882,
    "userId": "string",
    "verified": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="claim-domain-ownership-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Domain ownership successfully claimed.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="claim-domain-ownership-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|object|true|none|none|
|» boughtAt|number \| null|true|none|If it was purchased through Vercel, the timestamp in milliseconds when it was purchased.|
|» createdAt|number|true|none|Timestamp in milliseconds when the domain was created in the registry.|
|» creator|object|true|none|An object containing information of the domain creator, including the user's id, username, and email.|
|» » customerId|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » email|string|true|none|none|
|» » id|string|true|none|none|
|» » isDomainReseller|boolean|false|none|none|
|» » username|string|true|none|none|
|» customNameservers|[string]|false|none|A list of custom nameservers for the domain to point to. Only applies to domains purchased with Vercel.|
|» echMode|string|true|none|Whether the domain is enrolled in Encrypted Client Hello. `auto` leaves the decision to Vercel, `enabled` always enrolls, and `disabled` never enrolls and opts out of automatic enrollment.|
|» expiresAt|number \| null|true|none|Timestamp in milliseconds at which the domain is set to expire. null if not bought with Vercel.|
|» id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the domain.|
|» intendedNameservers|[string]|true|none|A list of the intended nameservers for the domain to point to Vercel DNS.|
|» name|string|true|none|The domain name.|
|» nameservers|[string]|true|none|A list of the current nameservers of the domain.|
|» renew|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the domain is set to automatically renew.|
|» serviceType|string|true|none|The type of service the domain is handled by. `external` if the DNS is externally handled, `zeit.world` if handled with Vercel, or `na` if the service is not available.|
|» teamId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» transferredAt|number \| null|false|none|Timestamp in milliseconds at which the domain was successfully transferred into Vercel. `null` if the transfer is still processing or was never transferred in.|
|» transferStartedAt|number|false|none|If transferred into Vercel, timestamp in milliseconds when the domain transfer was initiated.|
|» userId|string|true|none|none|
|» verified|boolean|true|none|If the domain has the ownership verified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» » isDomainReseller|false|
|» » isDomainReseller|true|
|» echMode|auto|
|» echMode|disabled|
|» echMode|enabled|
|» renew|false|
|» renew|true|
|» serviceType|external|
|» serviceType|na|
|» serviceType|zeit.world|
|» verified|false|
|» verified|true|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## List all the domains

<a id="opIdgetDomains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v5/domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v5/domains`

Retrieves a list of domains registered for the authenticated user or team. By default it returns the last 20 domains if no limit is provided.

<h3 id="list-all-the-domains-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|since|query|number|false|Get domains created after this JavaScript timestamp.|
|until|query|number|false|Get domains created before this JavaScript timestamp.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Add an existing domain to the Vercel platform

<a id="opIdcreateOrTransferDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v7/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example.com",
    "cdnEnabled": true,
    "zone": true,
    "method": "add"
  }'
```

`POST /v7/domains`

This endpoint is used for adding a new apex domain name with Vercel for the authenticating user. Note: This endpoint is no longer used for initiating domain transfers from external registrars to Vercel. For this, please use the endpoint [Transfer-in a domain](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/reference/endpoints/domains-registrar/transfer-in-a-domain).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example.com",
  "cdnEnabled": true,
  "zone": true,
  "method": "add"
}
```

<h3 id="add-an-existing-domain-to-the-vercel-platform-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» method|body|string|false|The domain operation to perform. It can be either `add` or `move-in`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|add|
|» name|body|string|true|The domain name you want to add.|
|» cdnEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the domain has the Vercel CDN enabled or not.|
|» zone|body|boolean|false|Whether to create a DNS zone on Vercel. Set `true` if using Vercel nameservers.|
|» method|body|string|false|The domain operation to perform.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|move-in|
|» name|body|string|true|The domain name you want to add.|
|» method|body|string|true|The domain operation to perform.|
|» token|body|string|false|The move-in token from Move Requested email.|

## Update or move apex domain

<a id="opIdpatchDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v3/domains/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "op": "update",
    "renew": true,
    "customNameservers": [
      "string"
    ],
    "zone": true,
    "echMode": "auto"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v3/domains/{domain}`

Update or move apex domain. Note: This endpoint is no longer used for updating auto-renew or nameservers. For this, please use the endpoints [Update auto-renew for a domain](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/reference/endpoints/domains-registrar/update-auto-renew-for-a-domain) and [Update nameservers for a domain](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/reference/endpoints/domains-registrar/update-nameservers-for-a-domain).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "op": "update",
  "renew": true,
  "customNameservers": [
    "string"
  ],
  "zone": true,
  "echMode": "auto"
}
```

<h3 id="update-or-move-apex-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|update|
|» op|body|string|false|none|
|» renew|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated. Please use PATCH /v1/registrar/domains/{domainName}/auto-renew instead.|
|» customNameservers|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated. Please use PATCH /v1/registrar/domains/{domainName}/nameservers instead.|
|» zone|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether this is a DNS zone that intends to use Vercel's nameservers.|
|» echMode|body|string|false|Encrypted Client Hello enrollment. 'auto' leaves it to Vercel, 'disabled' never enrolls and opts out of automatic enrollment.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|move-out|
|» op|body|string|false|none|
|» destination|body|string|false|User or team to move domain to|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» echMode|auto|
|» echMode|disabled|

```json
}
```

## Retrieves a list of all the Log Drains (deprecated)

<a id="opIdgetAllLogDrains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/log-drains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/log-drains`

Retrieves a list of all the Log Drains owned by the account. This endpoint must be called with an account AccessToken (integration OAuth2 clients are not allowed). Only log drains owned by the authenticated account can be accessed.

<h3 id="retrieves-a-list-of-all-the-log-drains-deprecated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|projectIdOrName|query|string|false|none|
|includeMetadata|query|boolean|false|none|
|includeDeliveryStats|query|boolean|false|Include `deliveryStats` with the delivery health of each drain over the last 24 hours. Ignored for teams without drain delivery metrics.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Creates a Configurable Log Drain (deprecated)

<a id="opIdcreateConfigurableLogDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/log-drains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "deliveryFormat": "json",
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "headers": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "projectIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "sources": [
      "static"
    ],
    "environments": [
      "preview"
    ],
    "secret": "string",
    "samplingRate": 0.01,
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/log-drains`

Creates a configurable log drain. This endpoint must be called with a team AccessToken (integration OAuth2 clients are not allowed)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deliveryFormat": "json",
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "headers": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "projectIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "sources": [
    "static"
  ],
  "environments": [
    "preview"
  ],
  "secret": "string",
  "samplingRate": 0.01,
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-configurable-log-drain-deprecated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» deliveryFormat|body|string|true|The delivery log format|
|» url|body|string(uri)|true|The log drain url|
|» headers|body|object|false|Headers to be sent together with the request|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» projectIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» sources|body|[string]|true|none|
|» environments|body|[string]|false|none|
|» secret|body|string|false|Custom secret of log drain|
|» samplingRate|body|number|false|The sampling rate for this log drain. It should be a percentage rate between 0 and 100. With max 2 decimal points|
|» name|body|string|false|The custom name of this log drain.|

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/integrations/log-drains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/integrations/log-drains`

Retrieves a list of all Integration log drains that are defined for the authenticated user or team. When using an OAuth2 token, the list is limited to log drains created by the authenticated integration.

<h3 id="retrieves-a-list-of-integration-log-drains-deprecated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "branch": "feature/*",
    "clientId": "oac_xRhY4LAB7yLhUADD69EvV7ct",
    "configurationId": "icfg_3bwCLgxL8qt5kjRLcv2Dit7F",
    "createdAt": 1558531915505,
    "createdFrom": "integration",
    "deliveryFormat": "json",
    "environments": [
      "production"
    ],
    "headers": "{\"Authorization\": \"Bearer 123\"}",
    "id": "ld_nBuA7zCID8g4QZ8g",
    "name": "My first log drain",
    "ownerId": "kr1PsOIzqEL5Xg6M4VZcZosf",
    "projectId": "AbCgVkqoxXeXCDWehVir51LHGrrcWL4mkYm14W6UBPWQeb",
    "projectIds": "AbCgVkqoxXeXCDWehVir51LHGrrcWL4mkYm14W6UBPWQeb",
    "samplingRate": 0.5,

  }
]
```

## Creates a new Integration Log Drain (deprecated)

<a id="opIdcreateLogDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/integrations/log-drains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My first log drain",
    "projectIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "secret": "a1Xsfd325fXcs",
    "deliveryFormat": "json",
    "url": "https://example.com/log-drain",
    "sources": [
      "static"
    ],
    "headers": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "environments": [
      "preview"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/integrations/log-drains`

Creates an Integration log drain. This endpoint must be called with an OAuth2 client (integration), since log drains are tied to integrations. If it is called with a different token type it will produce a 400 error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My first log drain",
  "projectIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "secret": "a1Xsfd325fXcs",
  "deliveryFormat": "json",
  "url": "https://example.com/log-drain",
  "sources": [
    "static"
  ],
  "headers": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "environments": [
    "preview"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-new-integration-log-drain-deprecated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the log drain|
|» projectIds|body|[string]|false|none|
|» secret|body|string|false|A secret to sign log drain notification headers so a consumer can verify their authenticity|
|» deliveryFormat|body|string|false|The delivery log format|
|» url|body|string(uri)|true|The url where you will receive logs. The protocol must be `https://` or `http://` when type is `json` and `ndjson`.|
|» sources|body|[string]|false|none|
|» headers|body|object|false|Headers to be sent together with the request|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» environments|body|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|» deliveryFormat|ndjson|
|» sources|static|
|» sources|lambda|
|» sources|build|
|» sources|edge|

|» sources|firewall|
|» environments|preview|
|» environments|production|

## Deletes the Integration log drain with the provided `id` (deprecated)

<a id="opIddeleteIntegrationLogDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/log-drains/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/integrations/log-drains/{id}`

Deletes the Integration log drain with the provided `id`. When using an OAuth2 Token, the log drain can be deleted only if the integration owns it.

<h3 id="deletes-the-integration-log-drain-with-the-provided-id-deprecated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID of the log drain to be deleted|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="deletes-the-integration-log-drain-with-the-provided-id-deprecated-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|The log drain was successfully deleted|None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

<h1 id="vercel-api-drains">drains</h1>

## Retrieve a list of all Drains

<a id="opIdgetDrains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/drains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/drains`

Allows to retrieve the list of Drains of the authenticated team.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-all-drains-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|includeMetadata|query|boolean|false|none|
|includeDeliveryStats|query|boolean|false|Include `deliveryStats` with the delivery health of each drain over the last 24 hours. Ignored for teams without drain delivery metrics.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "drains": [
    {
      "createdAt": 0,
      "delivery": {
        "compression": "gzip",
        "encoding": "json",

          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        },

        "type": "http"
      },

      "disabledReason": "account-plan-downgrade",

        "string"
      ],
      "sampling": [
        {
          "env": "preview",
          "rate": 0,
          "requestPath": "string",

        }

        "trace": {}
      },
      "source": {
        "defaultFor": "eve-tracing",
        "kind": "self-served"
      },
      "status": "disabled",
      "teamId": "string",
      "updatedAt": 0,
      "deliveryStats": {
        "attempts": 0,
        "failures": 0,
        "state": "failing",

        "filter": {
          "deployment": {
```

## Create a new Drain

<a id="opIdcreateDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/drains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "projects": "some",
    "projectIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "filter": {
      "version": "string",
      "filter": {
        "type": "string",
        "project": {
          "ids": [
            "string"
          ]
        },
        "log": {
          "sources": [
            "build"
          ]
        },
        "deployment": {
          "environments": [
            "production"
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    "schemas": {
      "property1": {
        "version": "string"
      },
      "property2": {
        "version": "string"
      }
    },
    "delivery": {
      "type": "string",
      "endpoint": "string",
      "compression": "gzip",
      "encoding": "json",
      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "secret": "string"
    },
    "sampling": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "rate": 0,
        "env": "production",
        "requestPath": "string"
      }
    ],
    "transforms": [
      {
        "id": "string"
      }
    ],
    "source": {
      "kind": "integration",
      "externalResourceId": "string"
    }
  }'
```

## Find a Drain by id

<a id="opIdgetDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/drains/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/drains/{id}`

Get the information for a specific Drain by passing the drain id in the URL.

<h3 id="find-a-drain-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|includeDeliveryStats|query|boolean|false|Include `deliveryStats` with the delivery health of the drain over the last 24 hours.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Delete a drain

<a id="opIddeleteDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/drains/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/drains/{id}`

Delete a specific Drain by passing the drain id in the URL.

<h3 id="delete-a-drain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="delete-a-drain-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|

|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

## Update an existing Drain

<a id="opIdupdateDrain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/drains/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "projects": "some",
    "projectIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "filter": "string",
    "schemas": {
      "property1": {
        "version": "string"
      },
      "property2": {
        "version": "string"
      }
    },
    "delivery": {
      "type": "string",
      "endpoint": "string",
      "compression": "gzip",
      "encoding": "json",
      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "secret": "string"
    },
    "sampling": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "rate": 0,
        "env": "production",
        "requestPath": "string"
      }
    ],
    "transforms": [
      {
        "id": "string"
      }
    ],
    "status": "enabled",
    "source": {
      "kind": "integration",
      "externalResourceId": "string"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
    ],
    "target": "production"
```

`POST /v1/edge-cache/invalidate-by-tags`

Marks a cache tag as stale, causing cache entries associated with that tag to be revalidated in the background on the next request.

## Dangerously delete by tag

<a id="opIddangerouslyDeleteByTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/edge-cache/dangerously-delete-by-tags?projectIdOrName=string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revalidationDeadlineSeconds": 0,
    "tags": [
      "string"
    ],
    "target": "production"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/edge-cache/dangerously-delete-by-tags`

Marks a cache tag as deleted, causing cache entries associated with that tag to be revalidated in the foreground on the next request. Use this method with caution because one tag can be associated with many paths and deleting the cache can cause many concurrent requests to the origin leading to cache stampede problem. This method is for advanced use cases and is not recommended; prefer using `invalidateByTag` instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revalidationDeadlineSeconds": 0,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "target": "production"
}
```

## Dangerously delete by source image

<a id="opIddangerouslyDeleteBySrcImages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/edge-cache/dangerously-delete-by-src-images?projectIdOrName=string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revalidationDeadlineSeconds": 0,
    "srcImages": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/edge-cache/dangerously-delete-by-src-images`

Marks a source image as deleted, causing cache entries associated with that source image to be revalidated in the foreground on the next request. Use this method with caution because one source image can be associated with many paths and deleting the cache can cause many concurrent requests to the origin leading to cache stampede problem. This method is for advanced use cases and is not recommended; prefer using `invalidateBySrcImage` instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revalidationDeadlineSeconds": 0,
  "srcImages": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="dangerously-delete-by-source-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrName|query|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» revalidationDeadlineSeconds|body|integer|false|none|
|» srcImages|body|[string]|true|none|

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/string/custom-environments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "string",

      "pattern": "string"

    "copyEnvVarsFrom": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v9/projects/{idOrName}/custom-environments`

Creates a custom environment for the current project. Cannot be named 'Production' or 'Preview'.

```json
{
  "slug": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "branchMatcher": {
    "type": "equals",
    "pattern": "string"
  },

}
```

## Update a custom environment

<a id="opIdupdateCustomEnvironment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/string/custom-environments/string \
  -X PATCH \
```

`PATCH /v9/projects/{idOrName}/custom-environments/{environmentSlugOrId}`

```json
  "description": "string",
```

<h1 id="vercel-api-user">user</h1>

## List User Events

<a id="opIdlistUserEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v3/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v3/events`

Retrieves a list of "events" generated by the User on Vercel. Events are generated when the User performs a particular action, such as logging in, creating a deployment, and joining a Team (just to name a few). When the `teamId` parameter is supplied, then the events that are returned will be in relation to the Team that was specified.

<h3 id="list-user-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|number|false|Maximum number of items which may be returned.|
|since|query|string|false|Timestamp to only include items created since then.|
|until|query|string|false|Timestamp to only include items created until then.|
|types|query|string|false|Comma-delimited list of event "types" to filter the results by.|
|userId|query|string|false|Deprecated. Use `principalId` instead. If `principalId` and `userId` both exist, `principalId` will be used.|
|principalId|query|string|false|When retrieving events for a Team, the `principalId` parameter may be specified to filter events generated by a specific principal.|
|projectIds|query|string|false|Comma-delimited list of project IDs to filter the results by.|
|entityId|query|string|false|Filters events to those associated with a specific entity (matched against `payload.id`). For example, a connector ID.|
|withPayload|query|string|false|When set to `true`, the response will include the `payload` field for each event.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "categories": [
        "deployment"
      ],
      "createdAt": 1632859321020,
      "details": [
        {
          "display": "inline",
          "label": "string",
          "value": "string"
        }
      ],
      "entities": [
        {
          "end": 3,
          "start": 0,
          "type": "author"
        }
      ],
      "id": "uev_bfmMjiMnXfnPbT97dGdpJbCN",
      "payload": {},
      "principal": {
        "avatar": "string",
        "email": "string",
        "slug": "string",
        "type": "user",
        "uid": "string",
        "username": "string"
      },
      "principalId": "string",
      "requestId": "string",
      "sessionId": "string",
      "summary": "string",
      "text": "You logged in via GitHub",
      "tokenId": "string",
      "type": "login",
      "user": {
        "avatar": "string",
        "email": "string",
        "slug": "string",
        "uid": "string",
        "username": "string"
      },

        }

        "string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Delete User Account

<a id="opIdrequestDelete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/user \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reasons": [
      {
        "slug": "string",
        "description": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /v1/user`

Initiates the deletion process for the currently authenticated User, by sending a deletion confirmation email. The email contains a link that the user needs to visit in order to proceed with the deletion process.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reasons": [
    {
      "slug": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-user-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reasons|body|[object]|false|Optional array of objects that describe the reason why the User account is being deleted.|
|» » slug|body|string|true|Idenitifier slug of the reason why the User account is being deleted.|
|» » description|body|string|true|Description of the reason why the User account is being deleted.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "email": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "message": "Verification email sent"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-user-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Response indicating that the User deletion process has been initiated, and a confirmation email has been sent.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized||None|
|402|Payment Required||None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="delete-user-account-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|string|true|none|Email address of the User who has initiated deletion.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier of the User who has initiated deletion.|
|message|string|true|none|User deletion progress status.|

<h1 id="vercel-api-feature-flags">feature-flags</h1>

## List flags

<a id="opIdlistFlagsV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/projects/string/feature-flags/flags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/projects/{projectIdOrName}/feature-flags/flags`

Retrieve feature flags for a project. Returns an opaque cursor for pagination.

<h3 id="list-flags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrName|path|string|true|The project id or name|
|state|query|string|false|The state of the flags to retrieve. Defaults to `active`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of flags to return.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Pagination cursor to continue from.|
|search|query|string|false|Search flags by their slug or description. Case-insensitive.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|Filter flags by tag. Repeat the parameter for multiple tags (all must match).|
|createdBy|query|string|false|Filter flags by the id of the entity that created them (a user or team id).|
|maintainerIds|query|[string]|false|Filter flags by maintainer user id. Repeat the parameter for multiple maintainers (any may match).|
|includeMarketplaceFlags|query|boolean|false|Whether to include Marketplace experimentation items in the paginated response. Defaults to false.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

|---|---|
|state|active|
|state|archived|

## List flags

<a id="opIdlistFlags"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/feature-flags/flags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/{projectIdOrName}/feature-flags/flags`

Retrieve feature flags for a project. The list can be filtered by state and supports pagination.

<h3 id="list-flags-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrName|path|string|true|The project id or name|
|state|query|string|false|The state of the flags to retrieve. Defaults to `active`.|
|withMetadata|query|boolean|false|Deprecated. Whether to include creator metadata in each flag in the response. Resolve creator identity client-side (e.g. via the team members endpoint) instead; this parameter will be removed in a future release. Use `GET /v1/projects/:id/feature-flags/flags/:flagIdOrSlug?withMetadata=true` for single-flag lookups that need creator metadata.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of flags to return. When not set, all flags are returned.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Pagination cursor to continue from.|
|search|query|string|false|Search flags by their slug or description. Case-insensitive.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|Filter flags by tag. Repeat the parameter for multiple tags (all must match).|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|active|
|state|archived|

## Get a flag

<a id="opIdgetFlag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/feature-flags/flags/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/{projectIdOrName}/feature-flags/flags/{flagIdOrSlug}`

Retrieve a specific feature flag by its ID or slug.

<h3 id="get-a-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrName|path|string|true|The project id or name|
|flagIdOrSlug|path|string|true|The flag id or name|
|ifMatch|query|string|false|Etag to match, can be used interchangeably with the `if-match` header|
|withMetadata|query|boolean|false|Whether to include metadata in the response|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|


`DELETE /v1/projects/{projectIdOrName}/feature-flags/flags/{flagIdOrSlug}`

Permanently delete a feature flag from the project. This action cannot be undone. Consider archiving the flag instead if you may need it in the future.

<h3 id="delete-a-flag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrName|path|string|true|The project id or name|
|flagIdOrSlug|path|string|true|The flag id or name|
|ifMatch|query|string|false|Etag to match, can be used interchangeably with the `if-match` header|
|withMetadata|query|boolean|false|Whether to include metadata in the response|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="delete-a-flag-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||None|
|304|Not Modified||None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|402|Payment Required|The account is missing a payment so payment method must be updated|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken

## List flag versions

<a id="opIdlistFlagVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/feature-flags/flags/string/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/{projectIdOrName}/feature-flags/flags/{flagIdOrSlug}/versions`

Lists flag versions for a given flag.

<h3 id="list-flag-versions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrName|path|string|true|none|
|flagIdOrSlug|path|string|true|none|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|cursor|query|string|false|Pagination cursor|
|environment|query|string|false|Environment to filter by|
|withMetadata|query|boolean|false|Whether to include metadata|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<a id="opIdcreateFlagSegment"></a>

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "string",
    "createdBy": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "data": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "id": "string",
          "conditions": [
            {
              "lhs": {
                "type": null
              },
              "cmp": "eq",
              "rhs": {
                "type": "list/inline",
                "items": [
                  {
                    "label": "string",
                    "note": "string",
                    "value": 0
                  }
                ]
              },
              "cmpOptions": {
```

## List git namespaces by provider

<a id="opIdgitNamespaces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/git-namespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/integrations/git-namespaces`

Lists git namespaces for a supported provider. Supported providers are `github`, `gitlab` and `bitbucket`. If the provider is not provided, it will try to obtain it from the user that authenticated the request.

<h3 id="list-git-namespaces-by-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|host|query|string|false|The custom Git host if using a custom Git provider, like GitHub Enterprise Server|
|provider|query|string|false|none|
|viewerMetadata|query|boolean|false|When true, includes the viewer object for each namespace.|

|provider|github-custom-host|
|provider|gitlab|
|provider|bitbucket|

## List git repositories linked to namespace by provider

<a id="opIdsearchRepo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/search-repo \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/integrations/search-repo`

Lists git repositories linked to a namespace `id` for a supported provider. A specific namespace `id` can be obtained via the `git-namespaces`  endpoint. Supported providers are `github`, `gitlab` and `bitbucket`. If the provider or namespace is not provided, it will try to obtain it from the user that authenticated the request.

<h3 id="list-git-repositories-linked-to-namespace-by-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|none|
|namespaceId|query|string \| number \| null|false|none|
|provider|query|string|false|none|
|installationId|query|string|false|none|
|host|query|string|false|The custom Git host if using a custom Git provider, like GitHub Enterprise Server|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|provider|github|
|provider|github-limited|
|provider|github-custom-host|
|provider|gitlab|
|provider|bitbucket|
|provider|cursor-origin|

## Connect integration resource to project

<a id="opIdconnectIntegrationResourceToProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/installations/string/resources/string/connections \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "projectId": "string",
    "envVarEnvironments": [
      "production"
    ],
    "makeEnvVarsSensitive": true
  }'
```

`POST /v1/integrations/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/resources/{resourceId}/connections`

Connects an integration resource to a Vercel project. This endpoint establishes a connection between a provisioned integration resource (from storage APIs like `POST /v1/storage/stores/integration/direct`) and a specific Vercel project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "projectId": "string",
  "envVarEnvironments": [
    "production"
  ],
  "makeEnvVarsSensitive": true
}
```

|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

## Delete an integration configuration

<a id="opIddeleteConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/configuration/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/integrations/configuration/{id}`

Allows to remove the configuration with the `id` provided in the parameters. The configuration and all of its resources will be removed. This includes Webhooks, LogDrains and Project Env variables.

<h3 id="delete-an-integration-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="delete-an-integration-configuration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|The configuration was successfully removed|None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found|The configuration was not found|None|
|410|Gone||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## List products for integration configuration

<a id="opIdgetConfigurationProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/configuration/icfg_cuwj0AdCdH3BwWT4LPijCC7t/products \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/integrations/configuration/{id}/products`

Returns products available for an integration configuration. Each product includes a `metadataSchema` field with the JSON Schema for required and optional metadata fields.

<h3 id="list-products-for-integration-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|ID of the integration configuration|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Create integration store (free and paid plans)

<a id="opIdcreateIntegrationStoreDirect"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/storage/stores/integration/direct \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-dev-database",
    "integrationConfigurationId": "icfg_cuwj0AdCdH3BwWT4LPijCC7t",
    "integrationProductIdOrSlug": "iap_postgres_db",
    "metadata": {
      "environment": "development",
      "project": "my-app",
      "tags": [
        "database",
        "postgres"
      ]
    },
    "externalId": "dev-db-001",
    "protocolSettings": {
      "experimentation": {
        "edgeConfigSyncingEnabled": true
      }
    },
    "source": "marketplace",
    "billingPlanId": "bp_abc123def456",
    "paymentMethodId": "pm_1AbcDefGhiJklMno",
    "prepaymentAmountCents": 5000
  }'
```

`POST /v1/storage/stores/integration/direct`

Creates an integration store with automatic billing plan handling. For free resources, omit `billingPlanId` to auto-discover free plans. For paid resources, provide a `billingPlanId` from the billing plans endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-dev-database",
  "integrationConfigurationId": "icfg_cuwj0AdCdH3BwWT4LPijCC7t",
  "integrationProductIdOrSlug": "iap_postgres_db",
  "metadata": {
    "environment": "development",
    "project": "my-app",
    "tags": [
      "database",
      "postgres"
    ]
  },
  "externalId": "dev-db-001",
  "protocolSettings": {
    "experimentation": {
      "edgeConfigSyncingEnabled": true
    }
  },
  "source": "marketplace",
  "billingPlanId": "bp_abc123def456",
  "paymentMethodId": "pm_1AbcDefGhiJklMno",
  "prepaymentAmountCents": 5000
}
```

<h3 id="create-integration-store-free-and-paid-plans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name for the storage resource|
|» integrationConfigurationId|body|string|true|ID of your integration configuration. Get this from GET /v1/integrations/configurations|
|» integrationProductIdOrSlug|body|string|true|ID or slug of the integration product. Get available products from GET /v1/integrations/configuration/{id}/products|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Product ID format|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Product slug format|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Optional key-value pairs for resource metadata|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| number \| boolean \| [string] \| [number]|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[number]|false|none|
|» externalId|body|string|false|Optional external identifier for tracking purposes|
|» protocolSettings|body|object|false|Protocol-specific configuration settings|
|» source|body|string|false|Source of the store creation request|
|» billingPlanId|body|string|false|ID of the billing plan for paid resources. Get available plans from GET /integrations/integration/{id}/products/{productId}/plans. If not provided, automatically discovers free billing plans.|
|» paymentMethodId|body|string|false|Payment method ID for paid resources. Optional - uses default payment method if not provided.|
|» prepaymentAmountCents|body|number|false|Amount in cents for prepayment billing plans. Required only for prepayment plans with variable amounts.|

## Rotate Installation Credential

<a id="opIdrotate-installation-credential"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/installations/string/credentials/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_secret": "string",
    "client_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/credentials/rotate`

Issues a replacement access token for an installation, so a partner can rotate a credential it believes is compromised without the customer having to reinstall. Authenticated by the credential being replaced plus the integration's client secret: a leaked access token on its own cannot rotate itself, which would otherwise let an attacker take over the installation and lock the partner out. The previous credential intentionally stays valid so in-flight requests keep working. Retiring it is a separate, explicit operation — a partner is never left mid-rotation without a working credential.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_secret": "string",
  "client_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-installation-credential-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|integrationConfigurationId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|none|
|» client_id|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "expires_in": 0,
  "scope": "string",
  "token_type": "oauth2-token"
}
```

<h3 id="rotate-installation-credential-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="rotate-installation-credential-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_token|string|true|none|none|
|expires_in|number|true|none|none|
|scope|string|true|none|none|
|token_type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|token_type|oauth2-token|

</aside>

## Revoke Installation Credential

<a id="opIdrevoke-installation-credential"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/installations/string/credentials/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "token": "string",
    "client_secret": "string",
    "client_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/credentials/revoke`

Retires a superseded installation credential, so a partner can complete a rotation it started with `POST /credentials/rotate` — the leaked credential stops working without the customer having to reinstall. Authenticated by a live installation credential plus the integration's client secret. The credential to retire is named in the body rather than being the one that authenticates, so the ordinary flow is: rotate, store the replacement, then authenticate with the replacement and revoke the old one. Refuses to retire an installation's last live credential. Rotation exists so remediation is not customer-visible; revoking the only credential would undo that and leave the install needing a reinstall.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "string",
  "client_secret": "string",
  "client_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-installation-credential-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|integrationConfigurationId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» token|body|string|true|none|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|none|
|» client_id|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "already_revoked": false,
  "revoked": false
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-installation-credential-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="revoke-installation-credential-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|revoked|boolean|true|none|none|

|already_revoked|true|

## Create Event

<a id="opIdcreate-event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/installations/string/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event": {
      "type": "installation.updated",
      "billingPlanId": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/events`

Partner notifies Vercel of any changes made to an Installation or a Resource. Vercel is expected to use `list-resources` and other read APIs to get the new state.<br/> <br/> `resource.updated` event should be dispatched when any state of a resource linked to Vercel is modified by the partner.<br/> `installation.updated` event should be dispatched when an installation's billing plan is changed via the provider instead of Vercel.<br/> <br/> Resource update use cases: <br/> <br/> - The user renames a database in the partner’s application. The partner should dispatch a `resource.updated` event to notify Vercel to update the resource in Vercel’s datastores.<br/> - A resource has been suspended due to a lack of use. The partner should dispatch a `resource.updated` event to notify Vercel to update the resource's status in Vercel's datastores.<br/>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event": {
    "type": "installation.updated",
    "billingPlanId": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|integrationConfigurationId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|

|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » productId|body|string|false|Partner-provided product slug or id|
|» » resourceId|body|string|true|Partner provided resource ID|

`PUT /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/resources/{resourceId}`

This endpoint imports (upserts) a resource to Vercel's installation. This may be needed if resources can be independently created on the partner's side and need to be synchronized to Vercel. When importing as part of the user-initiated import flow, call this endpoint before redirecting the user back to Vercel. See the [Import existing resources flow](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-flows#import-existing-resources-flow) for the full contract.

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/installations/string/billing \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "eod": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "period": {
      "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "billing": [
      {
        "billingPlanId": "string",
        "resourceId": "string",
        "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "name": "string",
        "details": "string",
        "price": "string",
        "quantity": 0,
        "units": "string",
        "total": "string"
      }
    ],
```

## Submit Invoice

<a id="opIdsubmit-invoice"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/installations/string/billing/invoices \
  -X POST \

    }

```

`POST /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/billing/invoices`

This endpoint allows the partner to submit an invoice to Vercel. The invoice is created in Vercel's billing system and sent to the customer. Depending on the type of billing plan, the invoice can be sent at a time of signup, at the start of the billing period, or at the end of the billing period.<br/> <br/> Use the `credentials.access_token` we provided in the [Upsert Installation](#upsert-installation) body to authorize this request. <br/> There are several limitations to the invoice submission:<br/> <br/> 1. A resource can only be billed once per the billing period and the billing plan.<br/> 2. The billing plan used to bill the resource must have been active for this resource during the billing period.<br/> 3. The billing plan used must be a subscription plan.<br/> 4. The interim usage data must be sent hourly for all types of subscriptions. See [Send subscription billing and usage data](#send-subscription-billing-and-usage-data) API on how to send interim billing and usage data.<br/> 5. If provided, `externalId` must be unique for the installation.<br/>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "externalId": "string",
  "invoiceDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "memo": "string",
  "period": {
    "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "items": [
    {
      "resourceId": "string",
      "billingPlanId": "string",
      "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "name": "string",
      "details": "string",
      "price": "string",
      "quantity": 0,
      "units": "string",
      "total": "string"
    }
  ],
  "discounts": [
    {
      "resourceId": "string",
      "billingPlanId": "string",
      "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "name": "string",
      "details": "string",
      "amount": "string"
    }
  ],
  "final": true,
  "test": {
    "validate": true,
    "result": "paid"
  }
}
```

`POST /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/billing/finalize`

This endpoint allows the partner to mark an installation as finalized. This means you will not send any more invoices for the installation. Use this after a customer has requested uninstall and you have sent any remaining invoices. This will allow the uninstall process to proceed immediately after all invoices have been paid. <br/> Use the `credentials.access_token` we provided in the [Upsert Installation](#upsert-installation) body to authorize this request.

`POST /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/billing/balance`

```json
{
```
```bash
  "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

      "credit": "string",
      "nameLabel": "string",
```

|» » resourceId|body|string|false|Partner's resource ID, exclude if credits are tied to the installation and not an individual resource.|

`PUT /v1/installations/{integrationConfigurationId}/products/{integrationProductIdOrSlug}/resources/{resourceId}/secrets`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

This endpoint is deprecated and replaced with the endpoint [Update Resource Secrets](#update-resource-secrets). <br/> This endpoint updates the secrets of a resource. If a resource has projects connected, the connected secrets are updated with the new secrets. The old secrets may still be used by existing connected projects because they are not automatically redeployed. Redeployment is a manual action and must be completed by the user. All new project connections will use the new secrets.<br/> <br/> Use cases for this endpoint:<br/> <br/> - Resetting the credentials of a database in the partner. If the user requests the credentials to be updated in the partner’s application, the partner post the new set of secrets to Vercel, the user should redeploy their application and the expire the old credentials.<br/>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "prefix": "string",
      "environmentOverrides": {
        "development": "string",
        "preview": "string",

      }
    }
  ],
  "partial": true
}
```

<h1 id="vercel-api-authentication">authentication</h1>

## SSO Token Exchange

<a id="opIdexchange-sso-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/sso/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "code": "string",
    "state": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_secret": "string",
    "redirect_uri": "string",
    "grant_type": "authorization_code"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/integrations/sso/token`

During the autorization process, Vercel sends the user to the provider [redirectLoginUrl](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/submit-integration#redirect-login-url), that includes the OAuth authorization `code` parameter. The provider then calls the SSO Token Exchange endpoint with the sent code and receives the OIDC token. They log the user in based on this token and redirects the user back to the Vercel account using deep-link parameters included the redirectLoginUrl. Providers should not persist the returned `id_token` in a database since the token will expire. See [**Authentication with SSO**](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api#authentication-with-sso) for more details.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "state": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_secret": "string",
  "redirect_uri": "string",
  "grant_type": "authorization_code"
}
```

<h3 id="sso-token-exchange-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» code|body|string|true|The sensitive code received from Vercel|
|» state|body|string|false|The state received from the initialization request|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The integration client id|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|The integration client secret|
|» redirect_uri|body|string|false|The integration redirect URI|
|» grant_type|body|string|true|The grant type, when using x-www-form-urlencoded content type|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» refresh_token|body|string|true|The refresh token received from previous token exchange|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The integration client id|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|The integration client secret|
|» grant_type|body|string|true|The grant type, when using x-www-form-urlencoded content type|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_type|authorization_code|
|» grant_type|refresh_token|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "string",
  "expires_in": 0,
  "id_token": "string",
  "refresh_token": "string",
  "token_type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="sso-token-exchange-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.|None|
|403|Forbidden||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

<h3 id="sso-token-exchange-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|access_token|string \| null|true|none|none|
|expires_in|number|false|none|none|
|id_token|string|true|none|none|
|refresh_token|string|false|none|none|
|token_type|string \| null|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|access_token|string|true|none|none|
|expires_in|number|true|none|none|
|id_token|string|true|none|none|
|refresh_token|string|true|none|none|
|token_type|string|true|none|none|

## Create an Auth Token

<a id="opIdcreateAuthToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v3/user/tokens \
  -X POST \

    "name": "string",
    "expiresAt": 0,
    "projectId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v3/user/tokens`

Creates and returns a new authentication token for the currently authenticated User. The `bearerToken` property is only provided once, in the response body, so be sure to save it on the client for use with API requests.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "expiresAt": 0,
  "projectId": "string"
}
```

|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» expiresAt|body|number|false|none|
|» projectId|body|string|false|The ID of the project to scope this token to|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "bearerToken": "uRKJSTt0L4RaSkiMj41QTkxM",

    "activeAt": 1632816536002,
    "createdAt": 1632816536002,
    "expiresAt": 1632816536002,
    "id": "5d9f2ebd38ddca62e5d51e9c1704c72530bdc8bfdd41e782a6687c48399e8391",
    "leakedAt": 1632816536002,
    "leakedUrl": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "origin": "github",
    "prefix": "vcp_",
    "revokedAt": 1632816536002,
    "scopes": [
      {
        "createdAt": 0,

        "origin": "app",

        },
        "type": "user"

    "suffix": "abc123",
    "type": "oauth2-token"
  }
}
```

`DELETE /v3/user/tokens/{tokenId}`

|logoutSource|vercel|

<h1 id="vercel-api-kms">kms</h1>

## Sign a message

<a id="opIdsignKmsMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/kms/issuers/string/sign/message \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "message": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/kms/issuers/{issuerId}/sign/message`

Sign a raw message with a KMS issuer's active signing key. Authenticate the request with a Vercel OIDC token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header; the issuer's policies decide which workloads are allowed to sign. The response `signature` is standard-base64 of the raw signature over the decoded message bytes. `keyId`, `algorithm`, and `fingerprint` identify the signing key in the issuer's JWKS.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="sign-a-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issuerId|path|string|true|The ID of the issuer.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» message|body|string|true|Base64-encoded message to be signed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "algorithm": "string",
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "keyId": "string",
  "signature": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="sign-a-message-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized||None|
|403|Forbidden||None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|429|Too Many Requests||None|

<h3 id="sign-a-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|algorithm|string|true|none|Algorithm of the signing key.|
|fingerprint|string|true|none|SHA-256 fingerprint of the signing key's public key (`SHA256:<base64>`).|
|keyId|string|true|none|Key id of the signing key. Matches the JWKS `kid` so verifiers can select the key after rotation without trial-verifying every published key.|
|signature|string|true|none|Standard-base64 encoding of the raw signature over the decoded message bytes.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

`POST /v1/kms/issuers/{issuerId}/sign/token`

Sign a JWT with a KMS issuer's active signing key. Authenticate the request with a Vercel OIDC token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header; the issuer's policies decide which workloads are allowed to sign. `keyId`, `algorithm`, and `fingerprint` identify the signing key in the issuer's JWKS.

```json
  "claims": {},

  "ttl": 300
```

|» claims|body|object|false|The claims to include in the token.|
|» headers|body|object|false|Additional headers to include in the token.|
|» ttl|body|number \| null|false|The time-to-live for the token, in seconds.|

```json
{
  "algorithm": "string",
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "keyId": "string",
  "token": "string"
}
```
