|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized||None|
|403|Forbidden||None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|429|Too Many Requests||None|

<h3 id="sign-a-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|algorithm|string|true|none|Algorithm of the signing key.|
|fingerprint|string|true|none|SHA-256 fingerprint of the signing key's public key (`SHA256:<base64>`).|
|keyId|string|true|none|Key id of the signing key. Matches the JWKS `kid` so verifiers can select the key after rotation without trial-verifying every published key.|
|token|string|true|none|Compact JWT signed by the issuer's active signing key.|

bearerToken
</aside>

<a id="opIdcreateKmsIssuer"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/kms/issuers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",

    "claimsSchema": {},
    "policy": {
      "kind": "project-grant",
      "teamId": "string",

        "string"
      ],
      "tokenClaims": {}
    },

    "importKeyId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/kms/issuers`

Create a new KMS issuer for the authenticated team, or for the team or organization identified by a Connect policy token. An issuer owns the asymmetric signing keys used to sign tokens and messages.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "algorithm": "RS512",
  "claimsSchema": {},
  "policy": {
    "kind": "project-grant",
    "teamId": "string",
    "projectId": "string",
    "environments": [
      "string"
    ],
    "tokenClaims": {}
  },
  "importKey": "string",
  "importKeyId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-issuer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the issuer.|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|The signing algorithm to use for the issuer.|
|» claimsSchema|body|object|false|A JSON Schema used to validate the resolved token claims when signing tokens for this issuer.|
|» policy|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » kind|body|string|true|none|
|» » teamId|body|string|true|The team ID for the project grant policy.|
|» » projectId|body|string|true|The project ID for the project grant policy.|
|» » environments|body|[string]|true|The environments for the project grant policy. Each entry is a system environment (production, preview, development) or a custom environment ID (env_...).|
|» » tokenClaims|body|object|false|The claims that KMS should include in signed JWTs for this policy.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » kind|body|string|true|none|
|» » clientId|body|string|true|The Connex client ID for the Connex grant policy.|
|» » tokenClaims|body|object|false|The claims that KMS should include in signed JWTs for this policy.|
|» importKey|body|string|false|The PEM-encoded private key to use for the issuer.|
|» importKeyId|body|string|false|The key id to use as the imported key's JWT/JWKS `kid`. Only allowed when `importKey` is provided. Not required to be unique; the addressable key id is the server-minted `keyId` returned in the response.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

## Create a signing key

<a id="opIdcreateKmsSigningKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/kms/issuers/string/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "activation": "automatic",
    "revokePreviousAfterHours": 0,
    "revokePreviousAt": "string",
    "importKey": "string",
    "importKeyId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/kms/issuers/{issuerId}/keys`

Create a new signing key for a KMS issuer. Depending on the activation mode, the key is activated automatically once its public key has propagated, or manually via the activate endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "activation": "automatic",
  "revokePreviousAfterHours": 0,
  "revokePreviousAt": "string",
  "importKey": "string",
  "importKeyId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-signing-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issuerId|path|string|true|The ID of the issuer.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» activation|body|string|false|Whether the new key is activated automatically after its public key has propagated, or manually via the activate endpoint. Defaults to `automatic`.|
|» revokePreviousAfterHours|body|number|false|For automatic activation, how many hours after activation the previous signing key should stop being used. Defaults to a 1 hour grace period so already-issued tokens keep verifying.|
|» revokePreviousAt|body|string \| number|false|Deprecated. The ISO date string or timestamp when the previous signing key should stop being used. Converted to a relative grace and applied at activation, not creation. Prefer revokePreviousAfterHours.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» importKey|body|string|false|The PEM-encoded private key to use for the issuer.|
|» importKeyId|body|string|false|The key id to use as the imported key's JWT/JWKS `kid`. Only allowed when `importKey` is provided. Not required to be unique; the addressable key id is the server-minted `keyId` returned in the response.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» activation|automatic|
|» activation|manual|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "activateAt": "string",
  "activatedAt": "string",
  "algorithm": "string",
  "certificatePem": "string",
  "createdAt": "string",
  "importKeyId": "string",
  "issuerId": "string",
  "keyId": "string",
  "publicKey": {
    "alg": "string",
    "key_ops": [
      "string"
    ],
    "kid": "string",
    "kty": "string",
    "use": "string",
    "x5c": [
      "string"
    ],
    "x5t#S256": "string"
  },
  "publicKeyFingerprint": "string",
  "publicKeyPem": "string",
  "revokeAt": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "updatedAt": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-signing-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|

## Activate a signing key

<a id="opIdactivateKmsSigningKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/kms/issuers/string/keys/string/activate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revokePreviousAfterHours": 0
  }'
```

`POST /v1/kms/issuers/{issuerId}/keys/{keyId}/activate`

Activate a pending signing key so the issuer starts signing with it.

```json
}
```

|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Get an issuer

<a id="opIdgetKmsIssuer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/kms/issuers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/kms/issuers/{issuerId}`

Retrieve a single KMS issuer by its ID. Accepts a team or organization bearer token, or an OIDC token authorized by one of the issuer's policies (e.g. a connex-grant token). The OIDC path returns the issuer without policies, since a policy token only proves signing access, not management access.

<h3 id="get-an-issuer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issuerId|path|string|true|The ID of the issuer.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
        "string"
      ],

      "updatedAt": "string"
    }
  ],
  "signingKeys": [
    {
      "activateAt": "string",
```

<h1 id="vercel-api-microfrontends">microfrontends</h1>

## List microfrontends groups

<a id="opIdgetMicrofrontendsGroups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/microfrontends/groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/microfrontends/groups`

Get the microfrontends group IDs for a team.

<h3 id="list-microfrontends-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="list-microfrontends-groups-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## List projects in a microfrontends group

<a id="opIdgetMicrofrontendsInGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/microfrontends/groups/string/projects \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/microfrontends/groups/{groupId}/projects`

Get the microfrontends for a given group ID.

<h3 id="list-projects-in-a-microfrontends-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Get microfrontends config for a deployment

<a id="opIdgetMicrofrontendsConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/microfrontends/string/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/microfrontends/{deploymentId}/config`

Get the microfrontends config for a deployment.

<h3 id="get-microfrontends-config-for-a-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deploymentId|path|string|true|The unique deployment identifier|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "config": {
    "$schema": "string",
    "applications": {
      "property1": {
        "development": {
          "fallback": "string",
          "local": "string",
          "task": "string"
        },
        "packageName": "string",
        "projectId": "string"
      },
      "property2": {
        "development": {
          "fallback": "string",
          "local": "string",
          "task": "string"
        },
        "packageName": "string",
        "projectId": "string"
      }
    },
    "options": {
      "disableOverrides": false,
      "localProxyPort": 0
    },
    "version": "1"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-microfrontends-config-for-a-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

<h3 id="get-microfrontends-config-for-a-deployment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|config|object \| null|true|none|projectIds are added when the config is uploaded to s3 deployment assets.|
|» $schema|string|false|none|See https://openapi.vercel.sh/microfrontends.json.|
|» applications|object|true|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|» » » development|object|true|none|Development configuration for the default application.|
|» » » » fallback|string|true|none|Fallback for local development, could point to any environment. This is required for the default app. This value is used as the fallback for child apps as well if they do not have a fallback. If passing a string, include the protocol (optional), host (required) and port (optional). For example: `https://this.ismyhost:8080`. If omitted, the protocol defaults to HTTPS. If omitted, the port defaults to `80` for HTTP and `443` for HTTPS. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.|
|» » » » local|string \| number|false|none|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|number|false|none|none|
|» » » » task|string|false|none|The task to run when starting the development server. Should reference a script in the package.json of the application. The default value is "dev". See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.|
|» » » packageName|string|false|none|The name used to run the application, e.g. the `name` field in the `package.json`. This is used by the local proxy to map the application config to the locally running app. This is only necessary when the application name does not match the `name` used in `package.json`. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/configuration#application-naming.|
|» » » projectId|string|true|none|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|» » » assetPrefix|string|false|none|The name of the asset prefix to use instead of the auto-generated name. The asset prefix is used to prefix all paths to static assets, such as JS, CSS, or images that are served by a specific application. It is necessary to ensure there are no conflicts with other applications on the same domain. An auto-generated asset prefix of the form `vc-ap-<hash>` is used when this field is not provided. When this field is provided, `/${assetPrefix}/:path*` must also be added to the list of paths in the `routing` field. Changing the asset prefix after a microfrontend application has already been deployed is not a forwards and backwards compatible change, and the asset prefix should be added to the `routing` field and deployed before setting the `assetPrefix` field. The default value is the auto-generated asset prefix of the form `vc-ap-<hash>`. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing#asset-prefix.|
|» » » development|object|false|none|Development configuration for the child application.|
|» » » » fallback|string|false|none|Fallback for local development, could point to any environment. If not provided for child apps, the fallback of the default app will be used. If passing a string, include the protocol (optional), host (required) and port (optional). For example: `https://this.ismyhost:8080`. If omitted, the protocol defaults to HTTPS. If omitted, the port defaults to `80` for HTTP and `443` for HTTPS. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.|
|» » » » local|string \| number|false|none|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|number|false|none|none|
|» » » » task|string|false|none|The task to run when starting the development server. Should reference a script in the package.json of the application. The default value is "dev". See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.|
|» » » packageName|string|false|none|The name used to run the application, e.g. the `name` field in the `package.json`. This is used by the local proxy to map the application config to the locally running app. This is only necessary when the application name does not match the `name` used in `package.json`. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/configuration#application-naming.|
|» » » routing|[object]|true|none|Groups of path expressions that are routed to this application. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing.|
|» » » » flag|string|false|none|The name of the feature flag that controls routing for this group of paths. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing#routing-changes-safely-with-flags.|
|» » » » group|string|false|none|Group name for the paths.|
|» » » » paths|[string]|true|none|A list of path expressions that are routed to this application. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/path-routing#supported-path-expressions.|
|» » » projectId|string|true|none|none|
|» options|object|false|none|Optional configuration options for the microfrontend.|
|» » disableOverrides|boolean|false|none|If you want to disable the overrides for the site. For example, if you are managing rewrites between applications externally, you may wish to disable the overrides on the toolbar as they will have no effect. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/managing-microfrontends/vercel-toolbar#routing-overrides.|
|» » localProxyPort|number|false|none|The port number used by the local proxy server. The default value is 3024. See https://vercel.com/docs/microfrontends/local-development.|
|» version|string|false|none|The version of the microfrontends config schema.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» » disableOverrides|false|
|» » disableOverrides|true|
|» version|1|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

`GET /v1/organizations`

## Create or Add Team to Organization

<a id="opIdaddOrganizationTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/string/teams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "mode": "create",
    "name": "string",
    "teamId": "string",
    "slug": "string",
    "billingPlan": "enterprise"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/teams`

Create a new team under an organization, or add an existing team. `mode: "create"` creates a brand-new child team from `slug` + `name` — a platform child by default, or an enterprise child (billed on the organization root's flex subscription) when `billingPlan: "enterprise"` is supplied. `mode: "link"` links an existing team identified by `teamId` or `slug`; the child's billing profile is derived from the target team's plan (enterprise team → enterprise child, else platform), or explicitly supplied. Both modes respond with the resulting organization-team link. This endpoint is in private beta. Contact your Vercel account team for access.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mode": "create",
  "name": "string",
  "teamId": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "billingPlan": "enterprise"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-add-team-to-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|The ID of the organization to create or add a team under.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» mode|body|string|true|Whether to create a new team under the organization (\"create\") or link an existing one (\"link\").|
|» teamId|body|string|false|The ID of an existing team to add to the organization (link mode).|
|» slug|body|string|false|The slug of an existing team to link, or the slug for a new team to create.|
|» name|body|string|false|The display name for a new team. Required in create mode; rejected in link mode.|
|» billingPlan|body|string|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» mode|body|string|true|none|
|» name|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» mode|body|string|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» mode|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|create|
|» mode|link|
|» billingPlan|enterprise|
|» billingPlan|platform|
|» mode|create|
|» mode|link|
|» mode|link|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "billingPlan": "enterprise",
  "createdAt": "string",
  "dsyncMode": "organization",
  "organizationId": "string",
  "ssoMode": "organization",
  "teamId": "string",
  "updatedAt": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-add-team-to-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[OrganizationTeam](#schemaorganizationteam)|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.<br>The slug is already in use|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|

## Stage routing rules

<a id="opIdstageRoutes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/routes \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "overwrite": true,
    "routes": []
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/projects/{projectId}/routes`

Stage routing rules for a project. Set `overwrite` to true to replace all existing rules, or omit it to merge with existing rules by ID. Returns the new staged version.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "overwrite": true,
  "routes": []
}
```

## Add a routing rule

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/routes \

    "route": {
      "name": "string",
```

`POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/routes`

Add a single routing rule to a project at a specified position. Defaults to the end of the list if no position is provided. The route is enabled by default. Stages a new version with the added route.

## Generate a routing rule from natural language

<a id="opIdgenerateRoute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/routes/generate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "string",
    "currentRoute": {
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "pathCondition": {
        "value": "string",
        "syntax": "string"
      },
      "caseSensitive": true,
      "conditions": [
        {
          "field": "string",
          "operator": "string",
          "key": "string",
          "value": "string",
          "missing": true
        }
      ],
      "actions": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "subType": "string",
          "dest": "string",
          "status": 0,
          "headers": [
            {
              "key": "string",
              "value": "string",
              "op": "string"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/routes/generate`

## Get routing rule version history

<a id="opIdgetRouteVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/routes/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/routes/versions`

Get the version history for a project's routing rules. Returns the staging version (if one exists) followed by production versions, most recent first. The staging version has `isStaging: true` and the current production version has `isLive: true`.

<h3 id="get-routing-rule-version-history-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "versions": [
    {
      "alias": "string",
      "createdBy": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "isLive": false,
      "isStaging": false,
      "lastModified": 0,
      "ruleCount": 0,
      "s3Key": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="get-routing-rule-version-history-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|versions|[object]|true|none|none|
|» alias|string|false|none|The staging alias for previewing this version.|
|» createdBy|string|true|none|The user who created this version.|
|» id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the version.|
|» isLive|boolean|false|none|Whether this version is currently live in production.|
|» isStaging|boolean|false|none|Whether this version is staged and not yet promoted to production.|
|» lastModified|number|true|none|Timestamp of when this version was last modified.|
|» ruleCount|number|false|none|The number of routing rules in this version.|
|» s3Key|string|true|none|The S3 key where the routing rules are stored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» isLive|false|
|» isLive|true|
|» isStaging|false|
|» isStaging|true|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Promote, restore, or discard a routing rule version

<a id="opIdupdateRouteVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/routes/versions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "string",
    "action": "promote"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/routes/versions`

Promote staged routing rules to production, restore a previous production version, or discard staged changes. - `promote`: Publishes the staging version to production. - `restore`: Rolls back to a previous production version. - `discard`: Removes the staging version without publishing.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "action": "promote"
}
```

<h3 id="promote-restore-or-discard-a-routing-rule-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|promote|
|» action|restore|
|» action|discard|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "version": {
    "alias": "string",
    "createdBy": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "isLive": false,
    "isStaging": false,
    "lastModified": 0,
    "ruleCount": 0,
    "s3Key": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="promote-restore-or-discard-a-routing-rule-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

<h3 id="promote-restore-or-discard-a-routing-rule-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|true|none|A version of routing rules stored in S3.|
|» alias|string|false|none|The staging alias for previewing this version.|
|» createdBy|string|true|none|The user who created this version.|
|» id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the version.|
|» isLive|boolean|false|none|Whether this version is currently live in production.|
|» isStaging|boolean|false|none|Whether this version is staged and not yet promoted to production.|
|» lastModified|number|true|none|Timestamp of when this version was last modified.|
|» ruleCount|number|false|none|The number of routing rules in this version.|
|» s3Key|string|true|none|The S3 key where the routing rules are stored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» isLive|false|
|» isLive|true|
|» isStaging|false|
|» isStaging|true|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

<h1 id="vercel-api-projects">projects</h1>

## Retrieve a list of projects

<a id="opIdgetProjects"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v10/projects`

Allows to retrieve the list of projects of the authenticated user or team. The list will be paginated and the provided query parameters allow filtering the returned projects.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string|false|Query only projects updated after the given timestamp or continuation token.|
|since|query|number|false|Query only projects updated after this JavaScript timestamp.|
|until|query|number|false|Query only projects updated before this JavaScript timestamp.|
|gitForkProtection|query|string|false|Specifies whether PRs from Git forks should require a team member's authorization before it can be deployed|
|limit|query|string|false|Limit the number of projects returned|
|search|query|string|false|Search projects by the name field|
|repo|query|string|false|Filter results by repo. Also used for project count|
|repoId|query|string|false|Filter results by Repository ID.|
|repoUrl|query|string|false|Filter results by Repository URL.|
|excludeRepos|query|string|false|Filter results by excluding those projects that belong to a repo|
|edgeConfigId|query|string|false|Filter results by connected Global Config ID|
|edgeConfigTokenId|query|string|false|Filter results by connected Global Config Token ID|
|deprecated|query|boolean|false|none|
|elasticConcurrencyEnabled|query|string|false|Filter results by projects with elastic concurrency enabled|
|staticIpsEnabled|query|string|false|Filter results by projects with Static IPs enabled|
|buildMachineTypes|query|string|false|Filter results by effective build machine types. Accepts comma-separated values. Use \"elastic\" for projects with elastic selection and \"default\" for projects without a build machine type set.|
|buildQueueConfiguration|query|string|false|Filter results by build queue configuration. SKIP_NAMESPACE_QUEUE includes projects without a configuration set.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|gitForkProtection|1|
|gitForkProtection|0|
|elasticConcurrencyEnabled|1|
|elasticConcurrencyEnabled|0|
|staticIpsEnabled|0|
|staticIpsEnabled|1|
|buildQueueConfiguration|SKIP_NAMESPACE_QUEUE|
|buildQueueConfiguration|WAIT_FOR_NAMESPACE_QUEUE|

|» » canaryResponseHeader|boolean|false|none|Whether the request served by a canary deployment should return a header indicating a canary was served. Defaults to `false` when omitted.|
|» » gate|object|false|none|Automated gating configuration. Omitted (the default) means no gating is configured, which is equivalent to `enabled: false`.|
|» » » action|string|true|none|What to do when the gate trips: pause the rollout, or roll it back.|
|» » » checks|[object]|true|none|The checks to evaluate. An empty array means nothing is evaluated.|
|» » » » excludePaths|[string]|false|none|Request paths to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Matched exactly against the request path with any query string removed; no prefix or glob matching. Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » » excludeStatusCodes|[number]|false|none|Response status codes to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » » ingestWatermarkSeconds|number|false|none|Seconds of ingest lag to allow for: the query's upper bound is `now() - this value`, so the check never reads a window that is still filling. Defaults to `30` when omitted.|
|» » » » significanceLevel|number|false|none|A run fails only when the canary's error rate is higher and its one-sided Fisher p-value is below this significance level. Defaults to `0.05`; lower values require stronger evidence.|
|» » » » type|string|true|none|The metric this check evaluates.|
|» » » dryRun|boolean|true|none|When true, a tripped gate is only reported — {@link action} is not taken.|
|» » » enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether automated gating is enabled for this project's rollouts.|
|» » » failureThreshold|number|false|none|How many failing evaluations within {@link windowSize} trip the gate. Defaults to `3` when omitted.|
|» » » windowSize|number|false|none|How many of the most recent evaluations {@link failureThreshold} is counted against. Defaults to `5` when omitted.|
|» » stages|[object]|false|none|An array of all the stages required during a deployment release. Each stage defines a target percentage and advancement rules. The final stage must always have targetPercentage: 100.|

## Get a project trace by request ID

<a id="opIdgetProjectTrace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/traces?projectId=prj_123&requestId=cli-req-abc' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/traces`

Returns the OTEL trace for a given Vercel CLI request.

<h3 id="get-a-project-trace-by-request-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|true|The project ID|
|requestId|query|string|true|The Vercel CLI request ID associated with the trace|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "trace": {
    "resources": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        },
        "name": "string"
      }
    ],
    "rootSpanId": "string",
    "spans": [
      {
        "attributes": {},
        "duration": [
          0,
          0
        ],
        "endTime": [
          0,
          0
        ],
        "events": [
          {
            "attributes": {},
            "name": "string",
            "timestamp": [
              0,
              0
            ]
          }
        ],
        "kind": 0,
        "library": {
          "name": "string",
          "version": "string"
        },
        "links": [
          {}
        ],
        "name": "string",
        "parentSpanId": "string",
        "resource": "string",
        "spanId": "string",
        "startTime": [
          0,
          0
        ],
        "status": {
          "code": 0,
          "message": "string"
        },
        "traceFlags": 0,
        "traceState": "string"
      }
    ],
    "traceId": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-project-trace-by-request-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

## Create a new project

<a id="opIdcreateProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v11/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enablePreviewFeedback": true,
    "enableProductionFeedback": true,
    "previewDeploymentsDisabled": true,
    "previewDeploymentSuffix": "string",
    "buildCommand": "string",
    "commandForIgnoringBuildStep": "string",
    "devCommand": "string",
    "environmentVariables": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "target": "production",
        "gitBranch": "string",
        "type": "system",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "framework": null,
    "gitRepository": {
      "repo": "string",
      "type": "github"
    },
    "installCommand": "string",
    "name": "a-project-name",
    "skipGitConnectDuringLink": true,
    "ssoProtection": {
      "deploymentType": "all"
    },
    "sandbox": {
      "region": "iad1",
      "failoverRegions": [
        "sfo1",
        "cle1"
      ]
    },
    "outputDirectory": "string",
    "publicSource": true,
    "rootDirectory": "string",
    "serverlessFunctionRegion": "stri",
    "serverlessFunctionZeroConfigFailover": true,
    "oidcTokenConfig": {
      "enabled": true,
      "issuerMode": "team"
    },
    "enableAffectedProjectsDeployments": true,
    "resourceConfig": {
      "buildMachineType": "standard",
      "fluid": true,
      "functionDefaultRegions": [
        "stri"
      ],
      "functionDefaultTimeout": 1,
      "functionDefaultMemoryType": "standard_legacy",
      "functionZeroConfigFailover": true,
      "elasticConcurrencyEnabled": true,
      "buildMachineSelection": "elastic",
      "buildMachineElasticLastUpdated": 0,
      "buildMachineElasticReason": "oom-failure",
      "buildMachineElasticTransition": {
        "at": 0,
        "direction": "upgrade",
        "algorithmVersion": "string"
      },
      "isNSNBDisabled": true,
      "buildQueue": {
        "configuration": "SKIP_NAMESPACE_QUEUE"
      },
      "enableFunctionsBeta": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v11/projects`

Allows to create a new project with the provided configuration. It only requires the project `name` but more configuration can be provided to override the defaults.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enablePreviewFeedback": true,
  "enableProductionFeedback": true,
  "previewDeploymentsDisabled": true,
  "previewDeploymentSuffix": "string",
  "buildCommand": "string",
  "commandForIgnoringBuildStep": "string",
  "devCommand": "string",
  "environmentVariables": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "target": "production",
      "gitBranch": "string",
      "type": "system",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "framework": null,
  "gitRepository": {
    "repo": "string",
    "type": "github"
  },
  "installCommand": "string",
  "name": "a-project-name",
  "skipGitConnectDuringLink": true,
  "ssoProtection": {
    "deploymentType": "all"
  },
  "sandbox": {
    "region": "iad1",
    "failoverRegions": [
      "sfo1",
      "cle1"
    ]
  },
  "outputDirectory": "string",
  "publicSource": true,
  "rootDirectory": "string",
  "serverlessFunctionRegion": "stri",
  "serverlessFunctionZeroConfigFailover": true,
  "oidcTokenConfig": {
    "enabled": true,
    "issuerMode": "team"
  },
  "enableAffectedProjectsDeployments": true,
  "resourceConfig": {
    "buildMachineType": "standard",
    "fluid": true,
    "functionDefaultRegions": [
      "stri"
    ],
    "functionDefaultTimeout": 1,
    "functionDefaultMemoryType": "standard_legacy",
    "functionZeroConfigFailover": true,
    "elasticConcurrencyEnabled": true,
    "buildMachineSelection": "elastic",
    "buildMachineElasticLastUpdated": 0,
    "buildMachineElasticReason": "oom-failure",
    "buildMachineElasticTransition": {
      "at": 0,
      "direction": "upgrade",
      "algorithmVersion": "string"
    },
    "isNSNBDisabled": true,
    "buildQueue": {
      "configuration": "SKIP_NAMESPACE_QUEUE"
    },
    "enableFunctionsBeta": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» enablePreviewFeedback|body|boolean \| null|false|Opt-in to preview toolbar on the project level|
|» enableProductionFeedback|body|boolean \| null|false|Opt-in to production toolbar on the project level|
|» previewDeploymentsDisabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Specifies whether preview deployments are disabled for this project.|
|» previewDeploymentSuffix|body|string \| null|false|Custom domain suffix for preview deployments. Takes precedence over team-level suffix. Must be a domain owned by the team.|
|» buildCommand|body|string \| null|false|The build command for this project. When `null` is used this value will be automatically detected|
|» commandForIgnoringBuildStep|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» devCommand|body|string \| null|false|The dev command for this project. When `null` is used this value will be automatically detected|
|» environmentVariables|body|[object]|false|Collection of ENV Variables the Project will use|
|» » key|body|string|true|Name of the ENV variable|
|» » target|body|string \| [string]|true|Deployment Target or Targets in which the ENV variable will be used|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » gitBranch|body|string|false|If defined, the git branch of the environment variable (must have target=preview)|
|» » type|body|string|false|Type of the ENV variable|
|» » value|body|string|true|Value for the ENV variable|
|» framework|body|null|false|The framework that is being used for this project. When `null` is used no framework is selected|
|» gitRepository|body|object|false|The Git Repository that will be connected to the project. When this is defined, any pushes to the specified connected Git Repository will be automatically deployed|
|» » repo|body|string|true|The name of the git repository. For example: \"vercel/next.js\"|
|» » type|body|string|true|The Git Provider of the repository|

|» name|body|string|true|The desired name for the project|
|» skipGitConnectDuringLink|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Opts-out of the message prompting a CLI user to connect a Git repository in `vercel link`.|

|» » deploymentType|body|string|true|none|

<h3 id="create-a-new-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The project was successfuly created|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.<br>At least one environment variable failed validation<br>The Bitbucket Webhook for the project link could not be created<br>The Gitlab Webhook for the project link could not be created|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|402|Payment Required|The account is missing a payment so payment method must be updated<br>Pro customers are allowed to deploy Serverless Functions to up to `proMaxRegions` regions, or if the project was created before the limit was introduced.<br>Deploying to Serverless Functions to multiple regions requires a plan update|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict|A project with the provided name already exists.|None|
|410|Gone||None|
|428|Precondition Required||None|
|429|Too Many Requests||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

## Generate a project OIDC token

<a id="opIdgetProjectToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/my-project%2C%20%3Cprj_id%3E/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "source": "vercel-cli:pull"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/token`

Generates an OIDC token for the project and returns it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source": "vercel-cli:pull"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-project-oidc-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The project ID or name|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» source|body|string|false|The source that is calling the endpoint.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-project-oidc-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="generate-a-project-oidc-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Create a trace session token for a deployment

<a id="opIdcreateTraceSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/traces/session \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "projectId": "string",
    "hostname": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects/traces/session`

Mints a short-lived HS256 JWT scoped to a deployment hostname. The Vercel CLI presents this JWT to the Vercel proxy on requests it wants traced.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "projectId": "string",
  "hostname": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-trace-session-token-for-a-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» projectId|body|string|true|The project ID the deployment belongs to.|
|» hostname|body|string|true|The deployment hostname to scope the trace session to.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-trace-session-token-for-a-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity||None|

<h3 id="create-a-trace-session-token-for-a-deployment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Find a project by id or name

<a id="opIdgetProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/prj_12HKQaOmR5t5Uy6vdcQsNIiZgHGB \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v9/projects/{idOrName}`

Get the information for a specific project by passing either the project `id` or `name` in the URL.

<h3 id="find-a-project-by-id-or-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

|» » » excludePaths|[string]|false|none|Request paths to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Matched exactly against the request path with any query string removed; no prefix or glob matching. Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » excludeStatusCodes|[number]|false|none|Response status codes to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|

|» » » significanceLevel|number|false|none|A run fails only when the canary's error rate is higher and its one-sided Fisher p-value is below this significance level. Defaults to `0.05`; lower values require stronger evidence.|

## Delete a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/prj_12HKQaOmR5t5Uy6vdcQsNIiZgHGB \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v9/projects/{idOrName}`

Delete a specific project by passing either the project `id` or `name` in the URL.

<h3 id="delete-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="delete-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|The project was successfuly removed|None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

|» commandForIgnoringBuildStep|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» customerSupportCodeVisibility|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether customer support can see git source for a deployment|

|» gitForkProtection|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether PRs from Git forks should require a team member's authorization before it can be deployed|
|» gitLFS|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether Git LFS is enabled for this project.|
|» protectedSourcemaps|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether sourcemaps are protected and require authentication to access.|
|» installCommand|body|string \| null|false|The install command for this project. When `null` is used this value will be automatically detected|

|» nodeVersion|body|string|false|none|
|» outputDirectory|body|string \| null|false|The output directory of the project. When `null` is used this value will be automatically detected|

|» previewDeploymentSuffix|body|string \| null|false|Custom domain suffix for preview deployments. Takes precedence over team-level suffix. Must be a domain owned by the team.|

<h3 id="update-an-existing-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The project was successfully updated|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.<br>Trusted IPs is only accessible for enterprise customers. This plan gate runs before the ACL check below on purpose: it depends only on the team's billing plan, so it can reject unsupported plans deterministically. `auth.can` resolves team membership (a DynamoDB lookup) and rejecting here first avoids depending on that external read for a request that is invalid regardless of authorization.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|402|Payment Required|The account is missing a payment so payment method must be updated<br>Pro customers are allowed to deploy Serverless Functions to up to `proMaxRegions` regions, or if the project was created before the limit was introduced.<br>Deploying to Serverless Functions to multiple regions requires a plan update|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict|The provided name for the project is already being used<br>The project is currently being transferred.|None|
|410|Gone||None|
|428|Precondition Required||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

## Upload a project avatar

<a id="opIduploadProjectAvatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/avatar \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/avatar`

Upload an image as the avatar of the project identified by `idOrName`. The request body is the raw bytes of a JPG, PNG, or SVG image; the `Content-Type` header must declare which. SVG payloads are sanitized and optimized server-side before storage. The final SHA-1 of the stored bytes becomes the project's `avatar` value. The actual upload pipeline (validation, sanitization, S3 write, conditional `updateProject`, and event emission) lives in the shared `@api/project-avatar-upload` helper so it can be reused by background workers.

<h3 id="upload-a-project-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|string(binary)|false|none|

## Delete a project avatar

<a id="opIddeleteProjectAvatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/avatar \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/projects/{idOrName}/avatar`

Remove the avatar of the project identified by `idOrName`. Deletes the chosen avatar field so the next production deploy can run auto-detection again. Does not delete the stored image.

<h3 id="delete-a-project-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Retrieve project domains by project by id or name

<a id="opIdgetProjectDomains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/string/domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v9/projects/{idOrName}/domains`

Retrieve the domains associated with a given project by passing either the project `id` or `name` in the URL.

<h3 id="retrieve-project-domains-by-project-by-id-or-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|production|query|string|false|Filters only production domains when set to `true`.|
|target|query|string|false|Filters on the target of the domain. Can be either "production", "preview"|
|customEnvironmentId|query|string|false|The unique custom environment identifier within the project|
|gitBranch|query|string|false|Filters domains based on specific branch.|

## Add a domain to a project

<a id="opIdaddProjectDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects/string/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "www.example.com",
    "gitBranch": null,
    "customEnvironmentId": "string",
    "redirect": "foobar.com",
    "redirectStatusCode": 307
  }'
```

`POST /v10/projects/{idOrName}/domains`

Add a domain to the project by passing its domain name and by specifying the project by either passing the project `id` or `name` in the URL. If the domain is not yet verified to be used on this project, the request will return `verified = false`, and the domain will need to be verified according to the `verification` challenge via `POST /projects/:idOrName/domains/:domain/verify`. If the domain already exists on the project, the request will fail with a `400` status code.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "www.example.com",
  "gitBranch": null,
  "customEnvironmentId": "string",
  "redirect": "foobar.com",
  "redirectStatusCode": 307
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-domain-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The project domain name|
|» gitBranch|body|string \| null|false|Git branch to link the project domain|
|» customEnvironmentId|body|string|false|The unique custom environment identifier within the project|
|» redirect|body|string \| null|false|Target destination domain for redirect|
|» redirectStatusCode|body|integer \| null|false|Status code for domain redirect|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

```json
    }

}
```

## Verify project domain

<a id="opIdverifyProjectDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/prj_12HKQaOmR5t5Uy6vdcQsNIiZgHGB/domains/example.com/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v9/projects/{idOrName}/domains/{domain}/verify`

Attempts to verify a project domain with `verified = false` by checking the correctness of the project domain's `verification` challenge.

<h3 id="verify-project-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|domain|path|string|true|The domain name you want to verify|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "apexName": "string",
  "createdAt": 0,
  "customEnvironmentId": "string",
  "gitBranch": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "projectId": "string",
  "redirect": "string",
  "redirectStatusCode": 301,
  "updatedAt": 0,
  "verified": false
}
```

<h3 id="verify-project-domain-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The project domain was verified successfully<br>Domain is already verified|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.<br>There is an existing TXT record on the domain verifying it for another project<br>The domain does not have a TXT record that attempts to verify the project domain<br>The TXT record on the domain does not match the expected challenge for the project domain<br>Project domain is not assigned to project|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="verify-project-domain-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apexName|string|true|none|none|
|createdAt|number|false|none|none|
|customEnvironmentId|string \| null|false|none|none|
|gitBranch|string \| null|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|projectId|string|true|none|none|
|redirect|string \| null|false|none|none|
|redirectStatusCode|number \| null|false|none|none|
|updatedAt|number|false|none|none|
|verified|boolean|true|none|`true` if the domain is verified for use with the project. If `false` it will not be used as an alias on this project until the challenge in `verification` is completed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|redirectStatusCode|301|
|redirectStatusCode|302|
|redirectStatusCode|307|
|redirectStatusCode|308|
|redirectStatusCode|null|
|verified|false|
|verified|true|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Retrieve the environment variables of a project by id or name

<a id="opIdfilterProjectEnvs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects/prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA/env \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v10/projects/{idOrName}/env`

Retrieve the environment variables for a given project by passing either the project `id` or `name` in the URL.

<h3 id="retrieve-the-environment-variables-of-a-project-by-id-or-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|gitBranch|query|string|false|If defined, the git branch of the environment variable to filter the results (must have target=preview)|
|decrypt|query|string|false|If true, the environment variable value will be decrypted|
|source|query|string|false|The source that is calling the endpoint.|
|customEnvironmentId|query|string|false|The unique custom environment identifier within the project|
|customEnvironmentSlug|query|string|false|The custom environment slug (name) within the project|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

|---|---|
|decrypt|true|
|decrypt|false|

## Create one or more environment variables

<a id="opIdcreateProjectEnv"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects/prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA/env \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "key": "API_URL",
    "value": "https://api.vercel.com",
    "type": "plain",
    "target": [
      "preview"
    ],
    "gitBranch": "feature-1",
    "comment": "database connection string for production",
    "customEnvironmentIds": [
      "env_1234567890"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v10/projects/{idOrName}/env`

Create one or more environment variables for a project by passing its `key`, `value`, `type` and `target` and by specifying the project by either passing the project `id` or `name` in the URL. If you include `upsert=true` as a query parameter, a new environment variable will not be created if it already exists but, the existing variable's value will be updated.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "key": "API_URL",
  "value": "https://api.vercel.com",
  "type": "plain",
  "target": [
    "preview"
  ],
  "gitBranch": "feature-1",
  "comment": "database connection string for production",
  "customEnvironmentIds": [
    "env_1234567890"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-or-more-environment-variables-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|upsert|query|string|false|Allow override of environment variable if it already exists|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object \| [object]|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» key|body|string|true|The name of the environment variable|

## Retrieve the decrypted value of an environment variable of a project by id

<a id="opIdgetProjectEnv"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA/env/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/env/{id}`

Retrieve the environment variable for a given project.

<h3 id="retrieve-the-decrypted-value-of-an-environment-variable-of-a-project-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|id|path|string|true|The unique ID for the environment variable to get the decrypted value.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "comment": "string",
  "configurationId": "string",
  "contentHint": {
    "storeId": "string",
    "type": "redis-url"
  },
  "createdAt": 0,
  "createdBy": "string",
  "customEnvironmentIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "decrypted": false,
  "edgeConfigId": "string",
  "edgeConfigTokenId": "string",
  "gitBranch": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "sunsetSecretId": "string",
  "target": [
    "development"
  ],
  "type": "encrypted",
  "updatedAt": 0,
  "updatedBy": "string",
  "visibility": "config"
}
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Remove an environment variable

<a id="opIdremoveProjectEnv"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA/env/XMbOEya1gUUO1ir4 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v9/projects/{idOrName}/env/{id}`

Delete a specific environment variable for a given project by passing the environment variable identifier and either passing the project `id` or `name` in the URL.

<h3 id="remove-an-environment-variable-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|id|path|string|true|The unique environment variable identifier|
|customEnvironmentId|query|string|false|The unique custom environment identifier within the project|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "comment": "string",
    "configurationId": "string",
    "contentHint": {
      "storeId": "string",
      "type": "redis-url"
    },
    "createdAt": 0,
    "createdBy": "string",
    "customEnvironmentIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "decrypted": false,
    "edgeConfigId": "string",
    "edgeConfigTokenId": "string",
    "gitBranch": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "internalContentHint": {
      "encryptedValue": "string",
      "type": "flags-secret"
    },
    "key": "string",
    "legacyValue": "string",
    "sunsetSecretId": "string",
    "target": [
      "development"
    ],
    "type": "encrypted",
    "updatedAt": 0,
    "updatedBy": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "visibility": "config"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="remove-an-environment-variable-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The environment variable was successfully removed|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict|The project is being transfered and removing an environment variable is not possible|None|
|410|Gone||None|

## Edit an environment variable

<a id="opIdeditProjectEnv"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA/env/XMbOEya1gUUO1ir4 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "key": "GITHUB_APP_ID",
    "target": [
      "preview"
    ],
    "gitBranch": "feature-1",
    "type": "plain",
    "value": "bkWIjbnxcvo78",
    "customEnvironmentIds": [
      "env_1234567890"
    ],
    "comment": "database connection string for production"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v9/projects/{idOrName}/env/{id}`

Edit a specific environment variable for a given project by passing the environment variable identifier and either passing the project `id` or `name` in the URL.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "key": "GITHUB_APP_ID",
  "target": [
    "preview"
  ],
  "gitBranch": "feature-1",
  "type": "plain",
  "value": "bkWIjbnxcvo78",
  "customEnvironmentIds": [
    "env_1234567890"
  ],
  "comment": "database connection string for production"
}
```

<h3 id="edit-an-environment-variable-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The unique project identifier or the project name|
|id|path|string|true|The unique environment variable identifier|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» key|body|string|false|The name of the environment variable|
|» target|body|[string]|false|The target environment of the environment variable|
|» gitBranch|body|string \| null|false|If defined, the git branch of the environment variable (must have target=preview)|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of environment variable|
|» value|body|string|false|The value of the environment variable|
|» customEnvironmentIds|body|[string]|false|The custom environments that the environment variable should be synced to|
|» comment|body|string|false|A comment to add context on what this env var is for|

## Create project transfer request

<a id="opIdcreateProjectTransferRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/projects/string/transfer-request \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "callbackUrl": "string",
    "callbackSecret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{idOrName}/transfer-request`

Initiates a project transfer request from one team to another. <br/> Returns a `code` that remains valid for 24 hours and can be used to accept the transfer request by another team using the `PUT /projects/transfer-request/:code` endpoint. <br/> Users can also accept the project transfer request using the claim URL: `https://vercel.com/claim-deployment?code=<code>&returnUrl=<returnUrl>`. <br/> The `code` parameter specifies the project transfer request code generated using this endpoint. <br/> The `returnUrl` parameter redirects users to a specific page of the application if the claim URL is invalid or expired.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "callbackUrl": "string",
  "callbackSecret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-project-transfer-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|The ID or name of the project to transfer.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» callbackUrl|body|string|false|The URL to send a webhook to when the transfer is accepted.|
|» callbackSecret|body|string|false|The secret to use to sign the webhook payload with HMAC-SHA256.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-project-transfer-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The project transfer request has been initiated successfully.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="create-project-transfer-request-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

## Accept project transfer request

<a id="opIdacceptProjectTransferRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/projects/transfer-request/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "newProjectName": "a-project-name",
    "paidFeatures": {
      "concurrentBuilds": 0,
      "passwordProtection": true,
      "previewDeploymentSuffix": true
    },
    "acceptedPolicies": {
      "property1": {
        "eula": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "privacy": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "property1": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "property2": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      },
      "property2": {
        "eula": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "privacy": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "property1": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "property2": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/transfer-request/{code}`

Accept a project transfer request initated by another team. <br/> The `code` is generated using the `POST /projects/:idOrName/transfer-request` endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "newProjectName": "a-project-name",
  "paidFeatures": {
    "concurrentBuilds": 0,
    "passwordProtection": true,
    "previewDeploymentSuffix": true
  },
  "acceptedPolicies": {
    "property1": {
      "eula": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "privacy": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "property1": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "property2": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "property2": {
      "eula": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "privacy": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "property1": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "property2": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="accept-project-transfer-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|code|path|string|true|The code of the project transfer request.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» newProjectName|body|string|false|The desired name for the project|
|» paidFeatures|body|object|false|none|
|» » concurrentBuilds|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » passwordProtection|body|boolean \| null|false|none|

|» » » privacy|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string(date-time)|false|none|

```json
    {
      "installationId": "string",

        "string"
      ],
      "result": {

      }
```

|» » secret|body|string|true|Automation bypass to revoked|
|» » regenerate|body|boolean|true|Whether or not a new automation bypass should be created after the provided secret is revoked|
|» generate|body|object|false|Generate a new secret. If neither generate or revoke are provided, a new random secret will be generated.|
|» » secret|body|string|false|Optional value of the secret to generate, don't send it for oauth2 tokens|
|» » note|body|string|false|Note to be displayed in the UI for this bypass|
|» update|body|object|false|Update an existing bypass|
|» » secret|body|string|true|Automation bypass to updated|
|» » isEnvVar|body|boolean|false|Whether or not this bypass is set as the VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET environment variable on deployments|
|» » note|body|string|false|Note to be displayed in the UI for this bypass|

```json
    },

    }

}
```

## Point production traffic to a previous production deployment by ID

<a id="opIdrequestRollback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/rollback/string \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/rollback/{deploymentId}`

Allows users to rollback to a deployment.

<h3 id="point-production-traffic-to-a-previous-production-deployment-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|deploymentId|path|string|true|The ID of the deployment to rollback *to*|
|description|query|string|false|The reason for the rollback|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="point-production-traffic-to-a-previous-production-deployment-by-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|402|Payment Required||None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity||None|

</aside>

## Update the microfrontends settings

<a id="opIdupdateMicrofrontends"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/prj_12HKQaOmR5t5Uy6vdcQsNIiZgHGB/microfrontends \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "microfrontendsGroupId": "mfe_12HKQaOmR5t5Uy6vdcQsNIiZgHGB",
    "enabled": true,
    "isDefaultApp": true,
    "defaultRoute": "/home",
    "routeObservabilityToThisProject": true,
    "doNotRouteWithMicrofrontendsRouting": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/projects/{projectId}/microfrontends`

Update the microfrontends settings for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "microfrontendsGroupId": "mfe_12HKQaOmR5t5Uy6vdcQsNIiZgHGB",
  "enabled": true,
  "isDefaultApp": true,
  "defaultRoute": "/home",
  "routeObservabilityToThisProject": true,
  "doNotRouteWithMicrofrontendsRouting": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-microfrontends-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|The unique project identifier|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» microfrontendsGroupId|body|string|false|The unique group identifier to add this microfrontend to|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable microfrontends for the project|
|» isDefaultApp|body|boolean|false|Whether the application is the default application for the microfrontends group|
|» defaultRoute|body|string|false|The default route used for screenshots and preview links for the project|
|» routeObservabilityToThisProject|body|boolean|false|Whether observability data should be routed to this project or a root project. Can only be set for child applications.|
|» doNotRouteWithMicrofrontendsRouting|body|boolean|false|Whether domains in this project should route as a microfrontend. Can only be set for child applications.|
