|» gate|object|false|none|Automated gating configuration. Omitted (the default) means no gating is configured, which is equivalent to `enabled: false`.|
|» » action|string|true|none|What to do when the gate trips: pause the rollout, or roll it back.|
|» » checks|[object]|true|none|The checks to evaluate. An empty array means nothing is evaluated.|
|» » » excludePaths|[string]|false|none|Request paths to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Matched exactly against the request path with any query string removed; no prefix or glob matching. Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » excludeStatusCodes|[number]|false|none|Response status codes to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » ingestWatermarkSeconds|number|false|none|Seconds of ingest lag to allow for: the query's upper bound is `now() - this value`, so the check never reads a window that is still filling. Defaults to `30` when omitted.|
|» » » significanceLevel|number|false|none|A run fails only when the canary's error rate is higher and its one-sided Fisher p-value is below this significance level. Defaults to `0.05`; lower values require stronger evidence.|
|» » » type|string|true|none|The metric this check evaluates.|
|» » dryRun|boolean|true|none|When true, a tripped gate is only reported — {@link action} is not taken.|
|» » enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether automated gating is enabled for this project's rollouts.|
|» » failureThreshold|number|false|none|How many failing evaluations within {@link windowSize} trip the gate. Defaults to `3` when omitted.|
|» » windowSize|number|false|none|How many of the most recent evaluations {@link failureThreshold} is counted against. Defaults to `5` when omitted.|
|» stages|[object]|false|none|An array of all the stages required during a deployment release. Each stage defines a target percentage and advancement rules. The final stage must always have targetPercentage: 100.|
|» » duration|number|false|none|Duration in minutes for automatic advancement to the next stage|
|» » linearShift|boolean|false|none|Whether to linearly shift traffic over the duration of this stage|
|» » requireApproval|boolean|false|none|Whether or not this stage requires manual approval to proceed|
|» » targetPercentage|number|true|none|The percentage of traffic to serve to the canary deployment (0-100)|

## Point production traffic to a given deployment

<a id="opIdrequestPromote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v10/projects/string/promote/string \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v10/projects/{projectId}/promote/{deploymentId}`

Allows users to promote a deployment to production. Note: This does NOT rebuild the deployment. If you need that, then call create-deployments endpoint.

<h3 id="point-production-traffic-to-a-given-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|none|
|deploymentId|path|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="point-production-traffic-to-a-given-deployment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||None|
|202|Accepted||None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>


|until|query|number|false|Get aliases created before this epoch timestamp.|

|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Pause a project

<a id="opIdpauseProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/pause`

Pause a project by passing its project `id` in the URL. If the project does not exist given the id then the request will fail with 400 status code. If the project disables auto assigning custom production domains and blocks the active Production Deployment then the request will return with 200 status code.

<h3 id="pause-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|string|true|The unique project identifier|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="pause-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerToken
</aside>

Unpause a project by passing its project `id` in the URL. If the project does not exist given the id then the request will fail with 400 status code. ## Get rolling release configuration

<a id="opIdgetRollingReleaseConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/rolling-release/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config`

Get the Rolling Releases configuration for a project. The project-level config is simply a template that will be used for any future rolling release, and not the configuration for any active rolling release.

<h3 id="get-rolling-release-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "rollingRelease": {
    "canaryResponseHeader": false,
    "gate": {
      "action": "pause",
      "checks": [
        {
          "excludePaths": [
            "/api/health"
          ],
          "excludeStatusCodes": [
            503
          ],
          "ingestWatermarkSeconds": 30,
          "significanceLevel": 0.05,
          "type": "error-rate-5xx"
        }
      ],
      "dryRun": false,
      "enabled": false,
      "failureThreshold": 3,
      "windowSize": 5
    },
    "stages": [
      {
        "duration": 600,
        "linearShift": false,
        "requireApproval": false,
        "targetPercentage": 25
      }
    ],
    "target": "production"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-rolling-release-configuration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="get-rolling-release-configuration-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rollingRelease|object \| null|true|none|Project-level rolling release configuration that defines how deployments should be gradually rolled out|
|» canaryResponseHeader|boolean|false|none|Whether the request served by a canary deployment should return a header indicating a canary was served. Defaults to `false` when omitted.|
|» gate|object|false|none|Automated gating configuration. Omitted (the default) means no gating is configured, which is equivalent to `enabled: false`.|
|» » action|string|true|none|What to do when the gate trips: pause the rollout, or roll it back.|
|» » checks|[object]|true|none|The checks to evaluate. An empty array means nothing is evaluated.|
|» » » excludePaths|[string]|false|none|Request paths to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Matched exactly against the request path with any query string removed; no prefix or glob matching. Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » excludeStatusCodes|[number]|false|none|Response status codes to ignore entirely — dropped from both the numerator (errors) and the denominator (total requests). Defaults to `[]` when omitted.|
|» » » ingestWatermarkSeconds|number|false|none|Seconds of ingest lag to allow for: the query's upper bound is `now() - this value`, so the check never reads a window that is still filling. Defaults to `30` when omitted.|
|» » » significanceLevel|number|false|none|A run fails only when the canary's error rate is higher and its one-sided Fisher p-value is below this significance level. Defaults to `0.05`; lower values require stronger evidence.|
|» » » type|string|true|none|The metric this check evaluates.|
|» » dryRun|boolean|true|none|When true, a tripped gate is only reported — {@link action} is not taken.|
|» » enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether automated gating is enabled for this project's rollouts.|
|» » failureThreshold|number|false|none|How many failing evaluations within {@link windowSize} trip the gate. Defaults to `3` when omitted.|
|» » windowSize|number|false|none|How many of the most recent evaluations {@link failureThreshold} is counted against. Defaults to `5` when omitted.|
|» stages|[object]|false|none|An array of all the stages required during a deployment release. Each stage defines a target percentage and advancement rules. The final stage must always have targetPercentage: 100.|
|» » duration|number|false|none|Duration in minutes for automatic advancement to the next stage|
|» » linearShift|boolean|false|none|Whether to linearly shift traffic over the duration of this stage|
|» » requireApproval|boolean|false|none|Whether or not this stage requires manual approval to proceed|
|» » targetPercentage|number|true|none|The percentage of traffic to serve to the canary deployment (0-100)|
|» target|string|true|none|The environment that the release targets, currently only supports production. Adding in case we want to configure with alias groups or custom environments.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» canaryResponseHeader|false|
|» canaryResponseHeader|true|
|» » action|pause|
|» » action|rollback|
|» » » type|error-rate-5xx|
|» » dryRun|false|
|» » dryRun|true|
|» » enabled|false|
|» » enabled|true|
|» » linearShift|false|
|» » linearShift|true|
|» » requireApproval|false|
|» » requireApproval|true|

</aside>

## Delete rolling release configuration

<a id="opIddeleteRollingReleaseConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/rolling-release/config \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config`

Disable Rolling Releases for a project means that future deployments will not undergo a rolling release. Changing the config never alters a rollout that's already in-flight—it only affects the next production deployment. If you want to also stop the current rollout, call this endpoint to disable the feature, and then call either the /complete or /abort endpoint.

<h3 id="delete-rolling-release-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Update the rolling release settings for the project

<a id="opIdupdateRollingReleaseConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/rolling-release/config \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PATCH /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config`

Update (or disable) Rolling Releases for a project. When disabling with the resolve-on-disable feature flag enabled, any active rolling release document is resolved using the disableRolloutAction parameter: "abort" to roll back (default), or "complete" to promote the canary to production. When enabling or updating config, changes only affect the next production deployment and do not alter a rollout that's already in-flight. Note: Enabling Rolling Releases automatically enables skew protection on the project with the default value if it wasn't configured already.

<h3 id="update-the-rolling-release-settings-for-the-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "rollingRelease": null
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|

## Start a rolling release for the project

<a id="opIdstartRollingRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/rolling-release/start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "canaryDeploymentId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/start`

Start a rolling release for a deployment. If a rolling release is already active for the same canary deployment, returns the current state without side effects.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "canaryDeploymentId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-rolling-release-for-the-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idOrName|path|string|true|Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» canaryDeploymentId|body|string|true|The ID of the canary deployment to start the rolling release for|

## Complete the rolling release for the project

<a id="opIdcompleteRollingRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/projects/string/rolling-release/complete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "canaryDeploymentId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/complete`

Force-complete a Rolling Release. The canary deployment will begin serving 100% of the traffic.

> Body parameter

```json

  "canaryDeploymentId": "string"
}
```

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» canaryDeploymentId|body|string|true|The ID of the canary deployment to complete|

<h1 id="vercel-api-sandboxes">sandboxes</h1>

## List sandboxes

<a id="opIdlistNamedSandboxes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/sandboxes`

Retrieves a paginated list of named sandboxes belonging to a specific project. Results can be sorted by creation time or name, and optionally filtered by name prefix or status. Overdue sessions for running and stopping sandboxes are recovered before returning the page, so an entry may no longer match its queried status after recovery.

<h3 id="list-sandboxes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|query|string|false|The unique identifier or name of the project to list named sandboxes for.|
|limit|query|number|false|Maximum number of named sandboxes to return in the response. Used for pagination.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|Field to sort by.|
|namePrefix|query|string|false|Filter named sandboxes whose name starts with this prefix. Only valid when sortBy=name.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sort direction. Defaults to desc.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter named sandboxes by status. Only valid when sortBy is createdAt.|
|tags|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter sandboxes by tag. Format: \"key:value\". Only one tag filter is supported at a time.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortBy|createdAt|
|sortBy|name|
|sortBy|statusUpdatedAt|
|sortBy|currentSnapshotId|
|sortOrder|asc|
|sortOrder|desc|
|status|running|
|status|stopping|
|status|stopped|

`POST /v2/sandboxes`

Creates a named sandbox environment. Named sandboxes have a unique name within a project and support automatic snapshotting on shutdown.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}`

Retrieves detailed information about a specific session, including its current status, resource configuration, and exposed routes.

<h3 id="get-a-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session to retrieve.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

    {
      "port": 0,
      "subdomain": "string",

      "url": "string"
```

## Get a named sandbox

<a id="opIdgetNamedSandbox"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/my-sandbox \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/sandboxes/{name}`

Retrieves a named sandbox by name, including its current sandbox and routes. If the sandbox is stopped and resume is true, a new sandbox will be created from the most recent snapshot. Returns 404 if the named sandbox or its configuration no longer exists.

<h3 id="get-a-named-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Name for the sandbox. Must be unique per project and URL-safe (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores).|
|projectId|query|string|false|The project ID or name (required when not using OIDC token).|
|resume|query|boolean|false|Whether to automatically resume a stopped named sandbox by creating a new instance from its snapshot. Defaults to false.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Delete a sandbox

<a id="opIddeleteSandbox"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/my-sandbox \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/sandboxes/{name}`

Deletes a sandbox by name. If sandboxes are currently running, they will be stopped first. This operation deletes all sandbox entities with the given name and the named sandbox metadata. When the config item is already missing, the returned sandbox uses stored metadata and defaults; config fields may be stale.

<h3 id="delete-a-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The sandbox name to delete.|
|projectId|query|string|false|The project ID that owns the named sandbox. When provided, takes precedence over OIDC project context.|
|deleteOrphanSnapshots|query|boolean|false|When true, snapshots of the deleted sandbox that are not referenced by any other sandbox are also deleted asynchronously. Defaults to false.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

<h3 id="update-a-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The sandbox to update.|
|projectId|query|string|false|The project ID that owns the named sandbox. When provided, takes precedence over OIDC project context.|
|resume|query|boolean|false|Whether to automatically resume a stopped named sandbox by creating a new instance from its snapshot. Defaults to false.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|» » memory|body|integer|false|The amount of memory in megabytes to allocate to the sandbox. Must equal vcpus * 2048.|
|» runtime|body|string|false|The runtime environment for the sandbox. Determines the pre-installed language runtimes and tools available.|

|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|

|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » deleteEvicted|body|boolean|false|Whether to immediately delete evicted snapshots. Defaults to true.|
|» networkPolicy|body|object|false|none|

|» » » » » » exact|body|string|false|Match the value exactly. Case-sensitive for paths, header values, and methods; case-insensitive for domains and header keys.|
|» » » » » » startsWith|body|string|false|Match values that start with the given prefix.|
|» » » » headers|body|[object]|false|Header matchers. Multiple entries are ANDed. Header names are compared case-insensitively (RFC 9110); header values are compared case-sensitively. When a request has multiple values for the same header, any matching value satisfies the matcher.|
|» » » » » key|body|object|false|Matcher for the entry key (header name or query key).|
|» » » » » » exact|body|string|false|Match the value exactly. Case-sensitive for paths, header values, and methods; case-insensitive for domains and header keys.|

## Execute a command

<a id="opIdrunSessionCommand"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/cmd \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "command": "npm",
    "args": [
      "install",
      "--save",
      "lodash"
    ],
    "cwd": "/home/vercel-sandbox",
    "env": {
      "NODE_ENV": "production",
      "DEBUG": "true"
    },
    "sudo": false,
    "wait": false,
    "logs": false,
    "timeout": 30000,
    "attachStdin": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/cmd`

Executes a shell command inside a running session. The command runs asynchronously and returns immediately with a command ID that can be used to track its progress and retrieve its output. Optionally, use the `wait` parameter to stream the command status until completion.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "command": "npm",
  "args": [
    "install",
    "--save",
    "lodash"
  ],
  "cwd": "/home/vercel-sandbox",
  "env": {
    "NODE_ENV": "production",
    "DEBUG": "true"
  },
  "sudo": false,
  "wait": false,
  "logs": false,
  "timeout": 30000,
  "attachStdin": false
}
```

<h3 id="execute-a-command-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session in which to execute the command.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» command|body|string|true|The executable or shell command to run. This is the program name without arguments.|
|» args|body|[string]|false|Arguments to pass to the command. Each argument should be a separate array element.|
|» cwd|body|string|false|The working directory in which to execute the command. Defaults to the sandbox home directory if not specified.|
|» env|body|object|false|Additional environment variables to set for this command. These are merged with the sandbox environment.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» sudo|body|boolean|false|Execute the command with root (superuser) privileges.|
|» wait|body|boolean|false|If true, returns an ND-JSON stream that emits the command status when started and again when finished. Useful for synchronously waiting for command completion.|
|» logs|body|boolean|false|If true, stream the logs of the command execution in real-time via ND-JSON. This is only applicable if `wait` is also true.|
|» timeout|body|integer|false|Maximum duration in milliseconds the command may run before it is killed with SIGKILL, up to 5 hours. Enforced at exec time, independently of `wait`.|
|» attachStdin|body|boolean|false|If true, keeps the command stdin open so it can be written to with the stdin endpoint while the command runs. When false, the command reads from an empty stdin.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "command": {
    "args": [
      "run",
      "build"
    ],
    "cwd": "/vercel/sandbox",
    "durationMs": 1234,
    "exitCode": 0,
    "id": "cmd_123a6c5209bc3778245d011443644c8d27dc2c50",
    "name": "npm",
    "sessionId": "sbx_123a6c5209bc3778245d011443644c8d27dc2c50",
    "startedAt": 1673123456789
  }
}
```

|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity||None|
|429|Too Many Requests||None|

## Kill a command

<a id="opIdkillSessionCommand"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/cmd/cmd_abc123/kill \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "signal": 15
  }'
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/cmd/{cmdId}/kill`

Sends a signal to terminate a running command in a session. The signal can be used to gracefully stop (SIGTERM) or forcefully kill (SIGKILL) the process. The command must still be running for this operation to succeed.

> Body parameter

```json

  "signal": 15
}
```

<h3 id="kill-a-command-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|cmdId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the command to terminate.|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session containing the command.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» signal|body|number|true|The POSIX signal number to send to the process. Common values: 15 (SIGTERM) for graceful termination, 9 (SIGKILL) for forced termination.|

```json
{
  "command": {
    "args": [
      "run",
      "build"

    "id": "cmd_123a6c5209bc3778245d011443644c8d27dc2c50",
    "name": "npm",
    "sessionId": "sbx_123a6c5209bc3778245d011443644c8d27dc2c50",

  }
}
```

## Write to command stdin

<a id="opIdwriteSessionCommandStdin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/cmd/cmd_abc123/stdin \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "data": "aGVsbG8K",
    "offset": 0,
    "close": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/cmd/{cmdId}/stdin`

Writes data to the stdin of a running command, and optionally closes it. The command must have been started with `attachStdin` set to true. Writes are applied in the order they are received. Send them one at a time to keep the data in order. A write returns once the command has accepted the data, and fails with a 504 after 30 seconds if the command is not reading stdin. Each write counts against the sandbox control plane rate limit, so batch small writes where possible. Set `offset` to the position in stdin where `data` starts to make a request safe to resend, for example after a 502 or 504: bytes the command has already received are skipped, and an offset past them fails with a 409. The response returns `bytesWritten`, the total written so far, and a 504 includes it in the error when the sandbox reports it. A request with no `data` and no `close` writes nothing and returns it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": "aGVsbG8K",
  "offset": 0,
  "close": false
}
```

<h3 id="write-to-command-stdin-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cmdId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the command to write to.|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session containing the command.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» data|body|string|false|Base64-encoded bytes to write to the command stdin. The request body is limited to 1 MB, so send at most about 700 KB of data per request.|
|» offset|body|integer|false|The position in the command stdin where `data` starts. Bytes before the total already written are skipped, so a resent request does not write them twice. Fails with 409 if it is past the bytes written so far. Without it, `data` is appended.|
|» close|body|boolean|false|If true, closes the command stdin after writing `data`. Use this for commands that wait for end of input.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "bytesWritten": 0,
  "command": {
    "args": [
      "run",
      "build"
    ],
    "cwd": "/vercel/sandbox",
```

## Stream command logs

<a id="opIdgetSessionCommandLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/cmd/cmd_abc123/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/cmd/{cmdId}/logs`

Streams the output of a command in real-time using newline-delimited JSON (ND-JSON). Each entry includes the output data and stream type. Stream types include `stdout`, `stderr`, and `error` (for stream failures).

<h3 id="stream-command-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session containing the command.|
|cmdId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the command to stream logs for.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

<h3 id="stream-command-logs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|

|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity||None|
|429|Too Many Requests||None|

## Stop a session

<a id="opIdstopSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/stop`

Stops a running session and releases its allocated resources. All running processes within the session will be terminated. This action cannot be undone. A stopped session cannot be restarted.

<h3 id="stop-a-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session to stop.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Extend session timeout

<a id="opIdextendSessionTimeout"></a>

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/extend-timeout`

Extends the maximum execution time of a running session. The session must be active and able to accept commands. The total timeout cannot exceed the maximum allowed limit for your account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "duration": 300000
}
```

|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» duration|body|number|true|The amount of time in milliseconds to add to the current timeout. Must be at least 1000ms (1 second).|

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/network-policy`

Replaces the network access policy of a running session. Use this to control which external hosts the session can communicate with. This is a full replacement. Any previously configured network rules will be overwritten.

> Body parameter

```json

    "*.npmjs.org"

    "104.16.0.0/12"
  ],
  "deniedCIDRs": [

  ],

      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "match": {
        "path": {
          "exact": "string",
          "startsWith": "string"
        },
        "method": [
          "string"
        ],

            "key": {
              "exact": "string",
              "startsWith": "string"
            },
            "value": {
              "exact": "string",
              "startsWith": "string"
            }

              "startsWith": "string"

      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/fs/read`

Downloads the contents of a file from a session's filesystem. The file content is returned as a binary stream with appropriate Content-Disposition headers for file download.

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cwd|body|string|false|The base directory for resolving relative paths. If not specified, paths are resolved from the sandbox home directory.|
|» path|body|string|true|The path of the file to read. Can be absolute or relative to the working directory.|

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/fs/mkdir`

Creates a new directory in a session's filesystem. By default, parent directories are created recursively if they don't exist (similar to `mkdir -p`).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cwd": "/home/vercel-sandbox",
  "path": "src/components",
  "recursive": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-directory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session to create the directory in.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» cwd|body|string|false|The base directory for resolving relative paths. If not specified, paths are resolved from the sandbox home directory.|
|» path|body|string|true|The path of the directory to create. Can be absolute or relative to the working directory.|
|» recursive|body|boolean|false|If true, creates parent directories as needed (like `mkdir -p`). If false, fails if parent directories do not exist.|

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/fs/write`

Uploads and extracts files to a session's filesystem. Files must be uploaded as a gzipped tarball (`.tar.gz`) with the `Content-Type` header set to `application/gzip`. The tarball contents are extracted to the session's working directory, or to a custom directory specified via the `x-cwd` header.

|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

```json
{}
```

## Create a snapshot

<a id="opIdcreateSandboxesSessionsBySessionIdSnapshotV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/snapshot \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expiration": null
  }'
```

`POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/snapshot`

Creates a point-in-time snapshot of a running session's filesystem. Snapshots can be used to quickly restore a session to a previous state or to create new sessions with pre-configured environments. The session must be running and able to accept commands for a snapshot to be created. The session will be terminated after the snapshot is created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiration": null
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session to snapshot.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expiration|body|object \| integer|false|The number of milliseconds after which the snapshot will expire and be deleted. Use 0 for no expiration.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|

`POST /v2/sandboxes/{name}/fork`

Forks a named sandbox, creating a new named sandbox from the source's configuration. Resources, timeout, ports, tags, network policy, mounts, Connect network, image, persistence, snapshot settings and — unlike the SDK-side fork — environment variables are copied from the source automatically (`interactive` is not). When the source has a snapshot the fork starts from it; otherwise it starts from the source's runtime/image. Any field provided in the request body overrides the value copied from the source.

`POST /v3/sandboxes`

Creates a named sandbox environment. Named sandboxes have a unique name within a project and support automatic snapshotting on shutdown. Unlike v2, this version has no `runtime` parameter: when no `image` is provided (and the sandbox is not restored from a snapshot), the sandbox is created from the default universal image.

## Create a snapshot

<a id="opIdcreateSandboxesSessionsBySessionIdSnapshotV3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v3/sandboxes/sessions/sbx_abc123/snapshot \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expiration": null
  }'
```

`POST /v3/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/snapshot`

Creates a point-in-time snapshot of a running session's filesystem. Snapshots can be used to quickly restore a session to a previous state or to create new sessions with pre-configured environments. The session must be running and able to accept commands for a snapshot to be created. The session will be terminated after the snapshot is created. Unlike v2, snapshots expire after 7 days when neither the request nor the sandbox configuration specifies an expiration.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiration": null
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-snapshot-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sessionId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the session to snapshot.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» expiration|body|object \| integer|false|The number of milliseconds after which the snapshot will expire and be deleted. Defaults to 7 days when neither this field nor the sandbox configuration specifies an expiration. Use 0 for no expiration.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|

`POST /v3/sandboxes/{name}/fork`

Forks a named sandbox, creating a new named sandbox from the source's configuration. Resources, timeout, ports, tags, network policy, mounts, Connect network, image, persistence, snapshot settings and — unlike the SDK-side fork — environment variables are copied from the source automatically (`interactive` is not). When the source has a snapshot the fork starts from it; otherwise it starts from the source's runtime/image. Any field provided in the request body overrides the value copied from the source. Unlike v2, when neither the body nor the source provides a value, snapshots expire after 7 days by default and persistent sandboxes keep only their most recent snapshot (`keepLastSnapshots: null` disables the limit).

`POST /v4/sandboxes`

Creates a named sandbox environment. Named sandboxes have a unique name within a project and support automatic snapshotting on shutdown. When no `image` is provided (and the sandbox is not restored from a snapshot), the sandbox is created from the default universal image. Unlike v3, snapshots expire after 7 days by default and persistent sandboxes keep only their most recent snapshot unless `keepLastSnapshots` is configured otherwise (or set to `null` to disable the limit).

|» » » allow|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » deny|body|[string]|false|none|
|» architecture|body|string|false|CPU architecture. Inherits a snapshot or single image manifest when omitted. Image indexes default to amd64. Must match the source. ARM64 creation requires API v3 or v4 without runtime and team access.|
|» resources|body|object|false|Resources to define the VM|
|» » vcpus|body|integer|false|The number of virtual CPUs to allocate to the sandbox. Must be 1, or an even number.|
|» » memory|body|integer|false|The amount of memory in megabytes to allocate to the sandbox. Must equal vcpus * 2048.|
|» source|body|object|false|The source from which to initialize the sandbox filesystem. Can be a Git repository, a tarball URL, or an existing snapshot.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Clone a Git repository into the sandbox.|
|» » type|body|object|true|Indicates the source is a Git repository.|
|» » url|body|string(uri)|true|The URL of the Git repository to clone.|
|» » username|body|string|false|Username for Git authentication. Required together with password for private repositories.|
|» » password|body|string|false|Password or personal access token for Git authentication. Required together with username for private repositories.|
|» » depth|body|integer|false|Create a shallow clone with history truncated to the specified number of commits. Useful for faster cloning of large repositories.|
|» » revision|body|string|false|The specific commit SHA, branch name, or tag to checkout after cloning.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Download and extract a gzipped tarball into the sandbox.|
|» » type|body|object|true|Indicates the source is a tarball.|
|» » url|body|string(uri)|true|URL of a gzipped tarball (.tar.gz) to download and extract.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Restore the sandbox filesystem from an existing snapshot.|
|» » type|body|object|true|Indicates the source is a snapshot.|
|» » snapshotId|body|string|true|The unique identifier of the snapshot to restore.|
|» projectId|body|string|false|The target project slug or ID in which the sandbox will be assigned to.|
|» ports|body|[integer]|false|List of ports to expose from the sandbox. Each port will be accessible via a unique URL. Maximum of 15 ports can be exposed.|
|» image|body|string|false|Image to use for the sandbox.|
|» timeout|body|integer|false|Maximum duration in milliseconds that the sandbox can run before being automatically stopped.|
|» env|body|object|false|Default environment variables for the sandbox. These are inherited by all commands unless overridden.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» mounts|body|object|false|List of drives to mount to the sandbox at the provided path.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » drive|body|string|true|Name of the drive to mount. The drive must already exist.|
|» » » mode|body|string|false|Mount the drive as read-write, or as a read-only snapshot. One writer is permitted at a time.|
|» region|body|string|false|The Vercel region in which to create the sandbox.|
|» failoverRegions|body|[string]|false|The regions the sandbox falls back to when it cannot be created in `region`.|
|» networkId|body|string|false|The Connect network id for the target Secure Compute private network.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name for the sandbox. Must be unique per project and URL-safe (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores).|
|» persistent|body|boolean|false|Whether the sandbox persists its state across restarts via automatic snapshots. Defaults to true.|
|» snapshotExpiration|body|object \| integer|false|Default snapshot expiration time in milliseconds. Defaults to 7 days. Set to 0 to disable expiration. When set, this value is used as the default expiration for all snapshots created for this sandbox.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» keepLastSnapshots|body|string \| object|false|Protect the N most recent snapshots with different expiration/deletion behavior. Persistent sandboxes default to keeping only the last snapshot (evicted snapshots are deleted). Set to null to disable the limit.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » count|body|integer|true|Number of most recent snapshots to keep.|
|» » expiration|body|object \| integer|false|Expiration time in milliseconds for kept snapshots. Falls back to snapshotExpiration.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » deleteEvicted|body|boolean|false|Whether to immediately delete evicted snapshots. Defaults to true.|
|» tags|body|object|false|Key-value tags to associate with the sandbox. Maximum 5 tags.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

<h1 id="vercel-api-security">security</h1>

## Update Attack Challenge mode

<a id="opIdupdateAttackChallengeMode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/attack-mode \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "projectId": "string",
    "attackModeEnabled": true,
    "attackModeActiveUntil": 0
  }'
```

`POST /v1/security/attack-mode`

Update the setting for determining if the project has Attack Challenge mode enabled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "projectId": "string",
  "attackModeEnabled": true,
  "attackModeActiveUntil": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-attack-challenge-mode-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» projectId|body|string|true|none|
|» attackModeEnabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» attackModeActiveUntil|body|number|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» projectId|body|string|true|none|
|» attackModeEnabled|body|boolean|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "attackModeEnabled": false,
  "attackModeUpdatedAt": 0
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

`PUT /v1/security/firewall/config`

Set the firewall configuration to provided rules and settings. Creates or overwrite the existing firewall configuration.

## Update Firewall Configuration

<a id="opIdupdateFirewallConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/firewall/config?projectId=string' \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action": "firewallEnabled",
    "id": null,
    "value": {
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "active": true,
      "conditionGroup": [
        {
          "conditions": [
            {
              "type": "host",
              "op": "re",
              "neg": true,
              "key": "string",
              "value": "string"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "action": {
        "mitigate": {
          "action": "deny"
        }
      },
      "valid": true,
      "validationErrors": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Read Firewall Configuration

<a id="opIdgetFirewallConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/firewall/config/string?projectId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/security/firewall/config/{configVersion}`

Retrieve the specified firewall configuration for a project. The deployed configVersion will be `active`

<h3 id="read-firewall-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|true|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|configVersion|path|string|true|The deployed configVersion for the firewall configuration|

|410|Gone||None|

## Returns activated WAF config

<a id="opIddeleteSecurityFirewallConfigByConfigVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/firewall/config/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /v1/security/firewall/config/{configVersion}`

Promotes a draft WAF config to an active config

<h3 id="returns-activated-waf-config-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|configVersion|path|string|true|The deployed configVersion for the firewall configuration|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
""
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||None|

|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|500|Internal Server Error||None|

## Read active attack data

<a id="opIdgetActiveAttackStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/firewall/attack-status?projectId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/security/firewall/attack-status`

Retrieve active attack data within the last N days (default: 1 day)

<h3 id="read-active-attack-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|true|none|
|since|query|number|false|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="read-active-attack-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permission to access this resource.|None|
|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

<h3 id="read-active-attack-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|anomalies|[object]|true|none|none|
|» affectedHostMap|object|true|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » » anomalyAlerts|object|false|none|none|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » » » » at_minute|string|true|none|none|
|» » » » » avg_requests|number|true|none|none|
|» » » » » stddev_requests|number|true|none|none|
|» » » » » total_requests_minute|number|true|none|none|
|» » » » » zscore|number|true|none|none|
|» » » ddosAlerts|object|false|none|none|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» » » » » atMinute|string|true|none|none|

## Read System Bypass

<a id="opIdgetBypassIp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/firewall/bypass?projectId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/security/firewall/bypass`

Retrieve the system bypass rules configured for the specified project

<h3 id="read-system-bypass-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|true|none|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|sourceIp|query|string|false|Filter by source IP|
|domain|query|string|false|Filter by domain|
|projectScope|query|boolean|false|Filter by project scoped rules|

## Read Firewall Actions by Project

<a id="opIdgetSecurityFirewallEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/security/firewall/events?projectId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/security/firewall/events`

Retrieve firewall actions for a project Rule names are resolved against the project's *current* active firewall configuration and the team's active rulesets, so a rule that has since been renamed reports its new name and one that has been deleted reports `null`. System rules such as `sys_dos_mitigation` and `ip_blocking` have no configured name and always report `null`. Filters (`ip`, `isActive`, `action`, `actionType`, `ruleKind`, `ruleId`, `hosts`) are ANDed across params and ORed within a repeated param. They are applied to the policies before `limit`/`cursor`, so pages only count matching policies. A policy with no matching requests yields no action row, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` actions; only `pagination.next` signals the end. A `cursor` is only valid with the filters it was issued for.

<h3 id="read-firewall-actions-by-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort|query|string|false|none|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|cursor|query|string|false|none|
|projectId|query|string|true|none|
|startTimestamp|query|number|false|none|
|endTimestamp|query|number|false|none|
|hosts|query|string|false|none|
|ip|query|[string]|false|none|
|isActive|query|boolean|false|none|
|action|query|[string]|false|none|
|actionType|query|[string]|false|none|
|ruleKind|query|string|false|none|
|ruleId|query|[string]|false|none|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|startTime:desc|
|sort|startTime:asc|
|action|deny|
|action|challenge|
|action|log|
|action|rate_limit|
|action|bypass|
|actionType|system-action|
|actionType|customer-action|
|ruleKind|system|
|ruleKind|custom|

> Example responses

```json
      "action": "string",

    }
  ],

  }
}
```

## List team members

<a id="opIdgetTeamMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v3/teams/team_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j1k2l/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v3/teams/{teamId}/members`

Get a paginated list of team members for the provided team.

<h3 id="list-team-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|number|false|Limit how many teams should be returned|
|since|query|number|false|Timestamp in milliseconds to only include members added since then.|
|until|query|number|false|Timestamp in milliseconds to only include members added until then.|
|search|query|string|false|Search team members by their name, username, and email.|
|role|query|string|false|Only return members with the specified team role.|
|excludeProject|query|string|false|Exclude members who belong to the specified project.|
|eligibleMembersForProjectId|query|string|false|Include team members who are eligible to be members of the specified project.|
|teamId|path|string|true|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Invite a user

<a id="opIdinviteUserToTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/teams/team_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j1k2l/members \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "role": "VIEWER",
      "projects": [
        {
          "projectId": "prj_ndlgr43fadlPyCtREAqxxdyFK",
          "role": "ADMIN"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /v2/teams/{teamId}/members`

Invite a user to join the team specified in the URL. The authenticated user needs to be an `OWNER` in order to successfully invoke this endpoint. The user to be invited must be specified by email.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "role": "VIEWER",
    "projects": [
      {
        "projectId": "prj_ndlgr43fadlPyCtREAqxxdyFK",
        "role": "ADMIN"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="invite-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|teamId|path|string|true|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|The email address of the user to invite|
|» role|body|string|false|The role of the user to invite|
|» projects|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » projectId|body|string|true|The ID of the project.|
|» » role|body|string|true|Sets the project roles for the invited user|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|OWNER|
|» role|MEMBER|
|» role|DEVELOPER|
|» role|SECURITY|
|» role|BILLING|
|» role|VIEWER|
|» role|VIEWER_FOR_PLUS|
|» role|CONTRIBUTOR|
|» » role|ADMIN|
|» » role|PROJECT_VIEWER|
|» » role|PROJECT_DEVELOPER|
|» » role|PROJECT_GUEST|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "email": "john@user.co",
  "role": "MEMBER",
  "teamPermissions": [
    "CreateProject"
  ],
  "teamRoles": [
    "MEMBER"
  ],
  "uid": "kr1PsOIzqEL5Xg6M4VZcZosf",
  "username": "john-doe"
}
```

<h3 id="invite-a-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[InvitedTeamMember](#schemainvitedteammember)|

|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|

|404|Not Found||None|
|410|Gone||None|

## Request access to a team

<a id="opIdrequestAccessToTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/teams/team_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j1k2l/request \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "joinedFrom": {
      "origin": "github",
      "commitId": "f498d25d8bd654b578716203be73084b31130cd7",
      "repoId": "67753070",
      "repoPath": "jane-doe/example",
      "gitUserId": 103053343,
      "gitUserLogin": "jane-doe"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/teams/{teamId}/request`

Request access to a team as a member. An owner has to approve the request. Only 100 users can request access to a team at the same time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "joinedFrom": {
    "origin": "github",
    "commitId": "f498d25d8bd654b578716203be73084b31130cd7",
    "repoId": "67753070",
    "repoPath": "jane-doe/example",
    "gitUserId": 103053343,

  }
}
```

## Get access request status

<a id="opIdgetTeamAccessRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/teams/team_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j1k2l/request/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/teams/{teamId}/request/{userId}`

Check the status of a join request. It'll respond with a 404 if the request has been declined. If no `userId` path segment was provided, this endpoint will instead return the status of the authenticated user.

`PATCH /v1/teams/{teamId}/members/{uid}`

Update the membership of a Team Member on the Team specified by `teamId`, such as changing the _role_ of the member, or confirming a request to join the Team for an unconfirmed member. The authenticated user must be an `OWNER` of the Team.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "confirmed": true,
  "role": "VIEWER",
  "teamPermissions": [
    "CreateProject",
    "FullProductionDeployment"
  ],
  "projects": [
    {
      "projectId": "prj_ndlgr43fadlPyCtREAqxxdyFK",
      "role": "ADMIN"
    }
  ],
  "joinedFrom": {
    "ssoUserId": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-team-member-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uid|path|string|true|The ID of the member.|
|teamId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» confirmed|body|boolean|false|Accept a user who requested access to the team.|
|» role|body|string|false|The role in the team of the member.|
|» teamPermissions|body|[string]|false|The team permissions to set for the member. Permissions must be compatible with the team roles assigned to the member.|
|» projects|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » projectId|body|string|true|The ID of the project.|
|» » role|body|string \| null|true|The project role of the member that will be added. \"null\" will remove this project level role.|
|» joinedFrom|body|object|false|none|
|» » ssoUserId|body|object \| null|false|none|

## List all teams

<a id="opIdgetTeams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v2/teams \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/teams`

Get a paginated list of all the Teams the authenticated User is a member of.

<h3 id="list-all-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|number|false|Maximum number of Teams which may be returned.|
|since|query|number|false|Timestamp (in milliseconds) to only include Teams created since then.|
|until|query|number|false|Timestamp (in milliseconds) to only include Teams created until then.|

## Delete a Team

<a id="opIddeleteTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/teams/team_1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j1k2l \
```

`DELETE /v1/teams/{teamId}`

Delete a team under your account. You need to send a `DELETE` request with the desired team `id`. An optional array of reasons for deletion may also be sent. Enterprise teams can only be deleted in test billing mode and when not linked to an organization. Enterprise children of an organization cannot be deleted.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reasons": [
    {
      "slug": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|newDefaultTeamId|query|string|false|Id of the team to be set as the new default team|
|teamId|path|string|true|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reasons|body|[object]|false|Optional array of objects that describe the reason why the team is being deleted.|
|» » slug|body|string|true|Idenitifier slug of the reason why the team is being deleted.|
|» » description|body|string|true|Description of the reason why the team is being deleted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "team_LLHUOMOoDlqOp8wPE4kFo9pE",
  "newDefaultTeamIdError": true
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-team-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The Team was successfully deleted|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|One of the provided values in the request body is invalid.<br>One of the provided values in the request query is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is not authorized.|None|
|402|Payment Required||None|

|404|Not Found||None|
|409|Conflict||None|
|410|Gone||None|
|503|Service Unavailable||None|

<h3 id="delete-a-team-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The ID of the deleted Team|
|newDefaultTeamIdError|boolean|false|none|Signifies whether the default team update has failed, when newDefaultTeamId is provided in request query.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|

|newDefaultTeamIdError|true|

|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

```json
null
```

## Get an invocation with its jobs and tasks

<a id="opIdgetVercelCiInvocationTree"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/vercel-ci/invocations/string/tree \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/vercel-ci/invocations/{invocationId}/tree`

Returns an invocation attempt together with every job definition, its latest job run, and the task definitions and active task runs of that job run. Defaults to the latest attempt when `attempt` is omitted. With `follow=1` the response is a newline-delimited JSON stream: a `{"type":"tree", ...}` event with the full tree is sent immediately and again whenever it changes, and a final `{"type":"end","reason":...}` event is sent when the attempt finishes (`completed`) or the stream reaches its maximum duration (`timeout`), after which clients should reconnect.

<h3 id="get-an-invocation-with-its-jobs-and-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invocationId|path|string|true|none|
|attempt|query|string|false|Invocation attempt to return. Defaults to the latest attempt.|
|follow|query|number|false|When 1, stream the tree as newline-delimited JSON until the attempt finishes.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|follow|0|
|follow|1|

## Get log lines for the tasks of an invocation attempt

<a id="opIdgetVercelCiTaskLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/vercel-ci/invocations/string/attempts/string/task-logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/vercel-ci/invocations/{invocationId}/attempts/{attempt}/task-logs`

Returns log lines for the tasks of an invocation attempt in a single request, grouped by task. Tasks can be narrowed by name and by conclusion, for example `conclusion=failed` to fetch only the logs of failed tasks. With `search`, every matching task is searched at once and only tasks with matching lines are returned.

<h3 id="get-log-lines-for-the-tasks-of-an-invocation-attempt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invocationId|path|string|true|none|
|attempt|path|string|true|none|
|task|query|[string]|false|Only return tasks with one of these names (e.g., \"web#test\").|
|conclusion|query|[string]|false|Only return completed tasks with one of these conclusions.|
|level|query|[string]|false|Only return log lines with one of these levels.|
|search|query|string|false|Only return log lines containing this text, ignoring case. Tasks without matching lines are left out, `limit` is ignored, and at most 1000 lines are returned.|
|limit|query|number|false|Maximum number of tasks to return (default: 10, max: 25).|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

## Search the task logs of several invocation attempts

<a id="opIdsearchVercelCiLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/vercel-ci/log-search?invocation=string&search=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/vercel-ci/log-search`

Searches the task logs of up to 50 invocation attempts at once, for example the most recent runs of a branch from `GET /v2/vercel-ci/invocations`. Only invocations and tasks with matching lines are returned. When more than 1000 lines match, the newest are kept.

<h3 id="search-the-task-logs-of-several-invocation-attempts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invocation|query|[string]|true|Invocation attempts to search, as \"<invocationId>:<attempt>\" (at most 50).|
|search|query|string|true|Only return log lines containing this text, ignoring case.|
|level|query|[string]|false|Only return log lines with one of these levels.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|level|trace|
|level|debug|
|level|command|
|level|info|
|level|warn|
|level|error|
|level|systemError|
|level|fatal|

<h1 id="vercel-api-web-analytics">web-analytics</h1>

## Aggregates page views

<a id="opIdaggregatePageviews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/query/web-analytics/visits/aggregate?projectId=prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA&by=day&by=country&since=2024-09-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z&until=2024-09-08T00%3A00%3A00.000Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/query/web-analytics/visits/aggregate`

Counts pageviews on a project, within the requested date range. Results are either aggregated or broken down over time. Results can additionally be broken down by one dimension, and filtered by multiple dimensions.

<h3 id="aggregates-page-views-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|true|The project identifier or the project name|
|by|query|[string]|true|Up to two dimensions used to break down results.<br><br>At most one time granularity is allowed: hour, day, week, month, year.<br><br>Other dimensions: country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm.<br><br>JSON dimensions: flags. Used bare, it breaks down results by key, for example flags returns one group per flag name. With a key, it breaks down results by that key's value, for example flags/beta_banner. Wrap keys containing characters other than letters, digits, and underscores in single quotes, for example flags/'my-flag'.|
|since|query|number \| string|true|Timestamp in milliseconds, or a valid Date string.<br><br>Selects data from (including) this date and time.<br>Will be adjusted according to the desired time granularity.|
|until|query|number \| string|true|Timestamp in milliseconds, or a valid Date string.<br><br>Selects data until (including) this date.<br>Will be adjusted according to the desired time granularity.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Number of distinct results, default to 10. Other results are grouped into "Others" group.|
|filter|query|string|false|OData-compliant filter. Encode the value when sending it in a URL.<br><br>Allows filtering on one or multiple dimensions. By default, filters for production environment only.<br><br>Supported dimensions: country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm.<br><br>JSON dimensions filtered by key: flags/<name>, for example flags/beta_banner eq 'true'. Wrap keys containing characters other than letters, digits, and underscores in single quotes, for example flags/'my-flag' eq 'true'.<br><br>Supported operations include eq, ne, in, and logical operators and, or, not with parentheses. Functions such as startswith are supported by the OData parser.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "browserName": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "deviceType": "string",
      "environment": "string",
      "flags": "string",
      "groupId": "string",
      "osName": "string",
      "projectId": "string",
      "projectName": "string",
      "referrerHostname": "string",
      "requestHostname": "string",

      "visitorId": "string",
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "query": {
    "filter": "string",
    "groupBy": [
      "string"
    ],
    "limit": 0,
    "since": "string",
    "until": "string"
  },
  "version": 0
}
```

## Aggregates custom events

<a id="opIdaggregateEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vercel.com/v1/query/web-analytics/events/aggregate?projectId=prj_XLKmu1DyR1eY7zq8UgeRKbA7yVLA&by=day&by=eventName&since=2024-09-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z&until=2024-09-08T00%3A00%3A00.000Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/query/web-analytics/events/aggregate`

Counts custom events on a project, within the requested date range. Results are either aggregated or broken down over time. Results can additionally be broken down by one dimension, and filtered by multiple dimensions.

<h3 id="aggregates-custom-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|true|The project identifier or the project name|
|by|query|[string]|true|Up to two dimensions used to break down results.<br><br>At most one time granularity is allowed: hour, day, week, month, year.<br><br>Other dimensions: country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm, eventName.<br><br>JSON dimensions: flags, eventData. Used bare, they break down results by key, for example flags returns one group per flag name. With a key, they break down results by that key's value, for example eventData/plan. Wrap keys containing characters other than letters, digits, and underscores in single quotes, for example flags/'my-flag'.|
|since|query|number \| string|true|Timestamp in milliseconds, or a valid Date string.<br><br>Selects data from (including) this date and time.<br>Will be adjusted according to the desired time granularity.|
|until|query|number \| string|true|Timestamp in milliseconds, or a valid Date string.<br><br>Selects data until (including) this date.<br>Will be adjusted according to the desired time granularity.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Number of distinct results, default to 10. Other results are grouped into "Others" group.|
|filter|query|string|false|OData-compliant filter. Encode the value when sending it in a URL.<br><br>Allows filtering on one or multiple dimensions. By default, filters for production environment only.<br><br>Supported dimensions: country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm, eventName.<br><br>JSON dimensions filtered by key: flags/<name>, eventData/<property>, for example eventData/plan eq 'pro'. Wrap keys containing characters other than letters, digits, and underscores in single quotes, for example flags/'my-flag' eq 'true'.<br><br>Supported operations include eq, ne, in, and logical operators and, or, not with parentheses. Functions such as startswith are supported by the OData parser.|
|teamId|query|string|false|The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.|
|slug|query|string|false|The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "browserName": "string",

      "string"
```

## Creates a webhook

<a id="opIdcreateWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vercel.com/v1/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "events": [
      "budget.reached"
    ],
    "projectIds": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/webhooks`

Creates a webhook

> Body parameter

```json

  "url": "http://example.com",
  "events": [

  ],

}
```

`GET /v2/deployments/{id}/aliases`
